## Architecture tiebreaker (settled from M1 — apply to any override note)

> Option C hybrid, narrowed. `useEntity(id)` is a READER, not authoritative loader. RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through `useAutoSaveSettings → useToolSettings` boundary. `createEntityStore` factory `load` parameter is for store-owned (non-server) entities only. Any RQ→store sync is boundary-internal, NEVER via consumer `useEffect(bootstrapEntity)` bridges. Constraint "useEntity lazy-loads on first mount" was DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise.

## Decision tree — ACT AUTONOMOUSLY (literal plan name, literal key every time)

### A. Chain state shows `complete` (all 5 milestones done) → SUCCESS EXIT
Report **"CHAIN M2-M6 COMPLETE"** loudly. List branches produced (`megaplan/m2-overlay-stack` ... `megaplan/m6-behavior-tests`). Remind human: branches not auto-pushed to GitHub (watchdog scope forbids it). `CronDelete` to stop loop.

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

### C. Active plan state=`critiqued` + next=`override add-note` (gate ESCALATE, known auto-crash)
Megaplan auto crashes trying to invoke `override add-note` as a phase. Apply tiebreaker verdict via `override replan`:
```
megaplan override replan --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "apply tiebreaker verdict" --note "TIEBREAKER VERDICT (Option C hybrid, narrowed, settled from M1): useEntity(id) is a READER not authoritative loader; RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through useAutoSaveSettings->useToolSettings boundary; createEntityStore factory load is for store-owned entities only; any RQ->store sync is boundary-internal NEVER consumer useEffect bridges. Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."
```
If gate ESCALATES a SECOND time on same plan despite the note (flag recurrence), force-proceed:
```
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "Gate ESCALATE recurring despite tiebreaker verdict and executor advisory; Claude review will catch real issues post-execute."
```
Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

### D. Active plan state=`executed` or `critiqued` with gate ESCALATE for reasons OTHER than tiebreaker architecture (FLAG-001/002/003-style concrete spec gaps)
Inspect gate.json for `unresolved_flags`. If flags name specific files/behaviors executor can address (e.g., "file X not in consumer list"), use `override add-note` with an advisory pointing at the concrete fix:
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTE ADVISORY: <specific files and pattern to handle, referencing the flag ID>"
```
Then `override force-proceed` to move forward. This worked on M1c FLAG-001 (useAddToVideoEditor null-safe-hook boundary).

### E. Execute phase returning `result=blocked` repeatedly (codex refusing browser/runtime tasks)
Inject the executor hard rule (if not already in plan metadata from init):
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTOR HARD RULE: browser/runtime-dependent tasks → return status=skipped on FIRST encounter, never status=blocked. Blocked retries waste iteration budget. deferred_human criteria get post-milestone manual verification."
```
This fixed M1b and M1c within 1-2 iterations after injection.

### F. Plan NOT advancing (no history entries in last 15 min, no codex proc, stale .plan.lock)
1. Remove stale lock: `rm /workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/<PLAN>/.plan.lock`
2. Restart chain tmux: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`

### G. Chain tmux session missing entirely (died unexpectedly)
Restart: `mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`. Verify `tmux ls` shows `chain` session. Check `chain.log` for why it died — if it hit `on_escalate: stop_chain` correctly, manually resolve that milestone first (sections C/D/E), then restart chain.

### H. Codex session poisoning (`bwrap: Creating new namespace failed` in exec.log, OR history shows >10 consecutive `result=blocked` with same artifact_hash)
```
rm -rf /root/.codex/sessions/*   # PRESERVE /root/.codex/auth.json
```
Then restart chain (section G). v0.14.6+ auto-detects this but if detection misses manual wipe works.

### I. Disk >90% full
```
find /tmp -name 'tmp*' -type f -mmin +240 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'supervise-*.log' -mtime +1 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'm0-exec.log' -mtime +1 -delete
```

### J. Codex auth lost (`codex login status` not "Logged in using ChatGPT")
STOP and report loud. Only human OAuth recovery. DO NOT re-auth from OPENAI_API_KEY.

### K. Supervisor STREAK with `error: argument --plan: expected one argument`
Variable-expansion bug. Shouldn't happen with megaplan chain (literal plan names), but if it does: look at the failing supervise log, manually relaunch supervisor for the active plan with LITERAL plan name + LITERAL API key hardcoded inline (no `$VAR` inside nested `bash -c '...'`).

## CONSTRAINTS (firm — violations cause incidents)

- NEVER edit `state.json` directly — use `megaplan override ...` commands
- NEVER push to remotes from container — branches are push-by-human-only
- NEVER re-auth codex from OPENAI_API_KEY env var
- NEVER delete `/root/.codex/auth.json`
- ALWAYS use literal plan names + literal API key in relaunch commands (past bug: `$PLAN` expanded empty in nested quoting)
- ALWAYS preserve uncommitted `.megaplan/plans/*` dirs during git operations
- Force-proceed is OK when: (1) gate ESCALATE recurring despite replan-with-verdict; (2) executor advisory note addresses the specific concrete flag; (3) 2+ rework cycles exhausted on same review feedback. NOT OK when: (1) first iteration with substantive gate flags that haven't been addressed; (2) you haven't inspected gate.json rationale.

## Report format (under 250 words)

(1) Chain status: milestone X of 5 (M2/M3/M4/M5/M6), current plan, state, iter.
(2) Progress since last fire: new phases completed, milestone transitions, rework cycles, new execute batches (count).
(3) Actions taken — list each with exact command run (literal names).
(4) Red flags that auto-resolved vs. still concerning.
(5) ETA to chain completion (remaining milestones × observed pace).

If healthy + advancing: one-line `chain healthy, milestone=<M?> plan=<name> state=<X> iter=<N> advancing`.

If you acted: describe the decision-tree branch taken and the command run.

The human does not need to be consulted for any branch A-I. Only J (codex auth lost) and ambiguous force-proceed cases require escalation.

## What we're doing (big picture)

**Project**: reigh-app state-management refactor, 2-week sprint compressed. Replace hook-chain / context-as-pubsub architecture with Zustand subscription-based stores to kill render storms that caused Model Select flash-close + textarea dropped keystrokes.

**Completed (on GitHub branch `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores`, commit `77bbb9340`)**:
- M0 render telemetry baseline
- M1 `createEntityStore` factory + `useJoinClipsSettings` port
- M1a settings-store rollout (`useAutoSaveSettings` over factory)
- M1b selection store (4 contexts → `selectionStore.ts`)
- M1c timeline store (3 contexts → `timelineStore.ts`)
- `fix: backfill defaults in createEntityStore seed` — prevents partial DB rows surfacing undefined fields

**Human verified in browser**: render counts dropped 15-20 → 1 on lightbox open; LightboxShell 31 → 1; SortableRow 0 renders during clip drag. Motivating bugs effectively dead.

**In flight — YOUR JOB TO DRIVE**: `megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh` running M2 → M3 → M4 → M5 → M6 autonomously on `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` base.

**Pending (by design)**: push per-milestone branches to GitHub (human will do post-chain); open PRs (human); M1a dependency audit of `useImageLightboxEnvironment` (nice-to-have, not blocking).

## Architecture tiebreaker (settled from M1 — apply to any override note)

> Option C hybrid, narrowed. `useEntity(id)` is a READER, not authoritative loader. RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through `useAutoSaveSettings → useToolSettings` boundary. `createEntityStore` factory `load` parameter is for store-owned (non-server) entities only. Any RQ→store sync is boundary-internal, NEVER via consumer `useEffect(bootstrapEntity)` bridges. Constraint "useEntity lazy-loads on first mount" was DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise.

## Decision tree — ACT AUTONOMOUSLY (literal plan name, literal key every time)

### A. Chain state shows `complete` (all 5 milestones done) → SUCCESS EXIT
Report **"CHAIN M2-M6 COMPLETE"** loudly. List branches produced (`megaplan/m2-overlay-stack` ... `megaplan/m6-behavior-tests`). Remind human: branches not auto-pushed to GitHub (watchdog scope forbids it). `CronDelete` to stop loop.

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

### C. Active plan state=`critiqued` + next=`override add-note` (gate ESCALATE, known auto-crash)
Megaplan auto crashes trying to invoke `override add-note` as a phase. Apply tiebreaker verdict via `override replan`:
```
megaplan override replan --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "apply tiebreaker verdict" --note "TIEBREAKER VERDICT (Option C hybrid, narrowed, settled from M1): useEntity(id) is a READER not authoritative loader; RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through useAutoSaveSettings->useToolSettings boundary; createEntityStore factory load is for store-owned entities only; any RQ->store sync is boundary-internal NEVER consumer useEffect bridges. Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."
```
If gate ESCALATES a SECOND time on same plan despite the note (flag recurrence), force-proceed:
```
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "Gate ESCALATE recurring despite tiebreaker verdict and executor advisory; Claude review will catch real issues post-execute."
```
Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

### D. Active plan state=`executed` or `critiqued` with gate ESCALATE for reasons OTHER than tiebreaker architecture (FLAG-001/002/003-style concrete spec gaps)
Inspect gate.json for `unresolved_flags`. If flags name specific files/behaviors executor can address (e.g., "file X not in consumer list"), use `override add-note` with an advisory pointing at the concrete fix:
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTE ADVISORY: <specific files and pattern to handle, referencing the flag ID>"
```
Then `override force-proceed` to move forward. This worked on M1c FLAG-001 (useAddToVideoEditor null-safe-hook boundary).

### E. Execute phase returning `result=blocked` repeatedly (codex refusing browser/runtime tasks)
Inject the executor hard rule (if not already in plan metadata from init):
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTOR HARD RULE: browser/runtime-dependent tasks → return status=skipped on FIRST encounter, never status=blocked. Blocked retries waste iteration budget. deferred_human criteria get post-milestone manual verification."
```
This fixed M1b and M1c within 1-2 iterations after injection.

### F. Plan NOT advancing (no history entries in last 15 min, no codex proc, stale .plan.lock)
1. Remove stale lock: `rm /workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/<PLAN>/.plan.lock`
2. Restart chain tmux: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`

### G. Chain tmux session missing entirely (died unexpectedly)
Restart: `mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`. Verify `tmux ls` shows `chain` session. Check `chain.log` for why it died — if it hit `on_escalate: stop_chain` correctly, manually resolve that milestone first (sections C/D/E), then restart chain.

### H. Codex session poisoning (`bwrap: Creating new namespace failed` in exec.log, OR history shows >10 consecutive `result=blocked` with same artifact_hash)
```
rm -rf /root/.codex/sessions/*   # PRESERVE /root/.codex/auth.json
```
Then restart chain (section G). v0.14.6+ auto-detects this but if detection misses manual wipe works.

### I. Disk >90% full
```
find /tmp -name 'tmp*' -type f -mmin +240 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'supervise-*.log' -mtime +1 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'm0-exec.log' -mtime +1 -delete
```

### J. Codex auth lost (`codex login status` not "Logged in using ChatGPT")
STOP and report loud. Only human OAuth recovery. DO NOT re-auth from OPENAI_API_KEY.

### K. Supervisor STREAK with `error: argument --plan: expected one argument`
Variable-expansion bug. Shouldn't happen with megaplan chain (literal plan names), but if it does: look at the failing supervise log, manually relaunch supervisor for the active plan with LITERAL plan name + LITERAL API key hardcoded inline (no `$VAR` inside nested `bash -c '...'`).

## CONSTRAINTS (firm — violations cause incidents)

- NEVER edit `state.json` directly — use `megaplan override ...` commands
- NEVER push to remotes from container — branches are push-by-human-only
- NEVER re-auth codex from OPENAI_API_KEY env var
- NEVER delete `/root/.codex/auth.json`
- ALWAYS use literal plan names + literal API key in relaunch commands (past bug: `$PLAN` expanded empty in nested quoting)
- ALWAYS preserve uncommitted `.megaplan/plans/*` dirs during git operations
- Force-proceed is OK when: (1) gate ESCALATE recurring despite replan-with-verdict; (2) executor advisory note addresses the specific concrete flag; (3) 2+ rework cycles exhausted on same review feedback. NOT OK when: (1) first iteration with substantive gate flags that haven't been addressed; (2) you haven't inspected gate.json rationale.

## Report format (under 250 words)

(1) Chain status: milestone X of 5 (M2/M3/M4/M5/M6), current plan, state, iter.
(2) Progress since last fire: new phases completed, milestone transitions, rework cycles, new execute batches (count).
(3) Actions taken — list each with exact command run (literal names).
(4) Red flags that auto-resolved vs. still concerning.
(5) ETA to chain completion (remaining milestones × observed pace).

If healthy + advancing: one-line `chain healthy, milestone=<M?> plan=<name> state=<X> iter=<N> advancing`.

If you acted: describe the decision-tree branch taken and the command run.

The human does not need to be consulted for any branch A-I. Only J (codex auth lost) and ambiguous force-proceed cases require escalation.

## Architecture tiebreaker (settled from M1 — apply to any override note)

> Option C hybrid, narrowed. `useEntity(id)` is a READER, not authoritative loader. RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through `useAutoSaveSettings → useToolSettings` boundary. `createEntityStore` factory `load` parameter is for store-owned (non-server) entities only. Any RQ→store sync is boundary-internal, NEVER via consumer `useEffect(bootstrapEntity)` bridges. Constraint "useEntity lazy-loads on first mount" was DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise.

## Decision tree — ACT AUTONOMOUSLY (literal plan name, literal key every time)

### A. Chain state shows `complete` (all 5 milestones done) → SUCCESS EXIT
Report **"CHAIN M2-M6 COMPLETE"** loudly. List branches produced (`megaplan/m2-overlay-stack` ... `megaplan/m6-behavior-tests`). Remind human: branches not auto-pushed to GitHub (watchdog scope forbids it). `CronDelete` to stop loop.

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

### C. Active plan state=`critiqued` + next=`override add-note` (gate ESCALATE, known auto-crash)
Megaplan auto crashes trying to invoke `override add-note` as a phase. Apply tiebreaker verdict via `override replan`:
```
megaplan override replan --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "apply tiebreaker verdict" --note "TIEBREAKER VERDICT (Option C hybrid, narrowed, settled from M1): useEntity(id) is a READER not authoritative loader; RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through useAutoSaveSettings->useToolSettings boundary; createEntityStore factory load is for store-owned entities only; any RQ->store sync is boundary-internal NEVER consumer useEffect bridges. Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."
```
If gate ESCALATES a SECOND time on same plan despite the note (flag recurrence), force-proceed:
```
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "Gate ESCALATE recurring despite tiebreaker verdict and executor advisory; Claude review will catch real issues post-execute."
```
Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

### D. Active plan state=`executed` or `critiqued` with gate ESCALATE for reasons OTHER than tiebreaker architecture (FLAG-001/002/003-style concrete spec gaps)
Inspect gate.json for `unresolved_flags`. If flags name specific files/behaviors executor can address (e.g., "file X not in consumer list"), use `override add-note` with an advisory pointing at the concrete fix:
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTE ADVISORY: <specific files and pattern to handle, referencing the flag ID>"
```
Then `override force-proceed` to move forward. This worked on M1c FLAG-001 (useAddToVideoEditor null-safe-hook boundary).

### E. Execute phase returning `result=blocked` repeatedly (codex refusing browser/runtime tasks)
Inject the executor hard rule (if not already in plan metadata from init):
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTOR HARD RULE: browser/runtime-dependent tasks → return status=skipped on FIRST encounter, never status=blocked. Blocked retries waste iteration budget. deferred_human criteria get post-milestone manual verification."
```
This fixed M1b and M1c within 1-2 iterations after injection.

### F. Plan NOT advancing (no history entries in last 15 min, no codex proc, stale .plan.lock)
1. Remove stale lock: `rm /workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/<PLAN>/.plan.lock`
2. Restart chain tmux: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`

### G. Chain tmux session missing entirely (died unexpectedly)
Restart: `mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`. Verify `tmux ls` shows `chain` session. Check `chain.log` for why it died — if it hit `on_escalate: stop_chain` correctly, manually resolve that milestone first (sections C/D/E), then restart chain.

### H. Codex session poisoning (`bwrap: Creating new namespace failed` in exec.log, OR history shows >10 consecutive `result=blocked` with same artifact_hash)
```
rm -rf /root/.codex/sessions/*   # PRESERVE /root/.codex/auth.json
```
Then restart chain (section G). v0.14.6+ auto-detects this but if detection misses manual wipe works.

### I. Disk >90% full
```
find /tmp -name 'tmp*' -type f -mmin +240 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'supervise-*.log' -mtime +1 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'm0-exec.log' -mtime +1 -delete
```

### J. Codex auth lost (`codex login status` not "Logged in using ChatGPT")
STOP and report loud. Only human OAuth recovery. DO NOT re-auth from OPENAI_API_KEY.

### K. Supervisor STREAK with `error: argument --plan: expected one argument`
Variable-expansion bug. Shouldn't happen with megaplan chain (literal plan names), but if it does: look at the failing supervise log, manually relaunch supervisor for the active plan with LITERAL plan name + LITERAL API key hardcoded inline (no `$VAR` inside nested `bash -c '...'`).

## CONSTRAINTS (firm — violations cause incidents)

- NEVER edit `state.json` directly — use `megaplan override ...` commands
- NEVER push to remotes from container — branches are push-by-human-only
- NEVER re-auth codex from OPENAI_API_KEY env var
- NEVER delete `/root/.codex/auth.json`
- ALWAYS use literal plan names + literal API key in relaunch commands (past bug: `$PLAN` expanded empty in nested quoting)
- ALWAYS preserve uncommitted `.megaplan/plans/*` dirs during git operations
- Force-proceed is OK when: (1) gate ESCALATE recurring despite replan-with-verdict; (2) executor advisory note addresses the specific concrete flag; (3) 2+ rework cycles exhausted on same review feedback. NOT OK when: (1) first iteration with substantive gate flags that haven't been addressed; (2) you haven't inspected gate.json rationale.

(1) Chain status: milestone X of 5 (M2/M3/M4/M5/M6), current plan, state, iter.
(2) Progress since last fire: new phases completed, milestone transitions, rework cycles, new execute batches (count).
(3) Actions taken — list each with exact command run (literal names).
(4) Red flags that auto-resolved vs. still concerning.
(5) ETA to chain completion (remaining milestones × observed pace).

If healthy + advancing: one-line `chain healthy, milestone=<M?> plan=<name> state=<X> iter=<N> advancing`.

If you acted: describe the decision-tree branch taken and the command run.

The human does not need to be consulted for any branch A-I. Only J (codex auth lost) and ambiguous force-proceed cases require escalation.

**Human verified in browser**: render counts dropped 15-20 → 1 on lightbox open; LightboxShell 31 → 1; SortableRow 0 renders during clip drag. Motivating bugs effectively dead.

**In flight — YOUR JOB TO DRIVE**: `megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh` running M2 → M3 → M4 → M5 → M6 autonomously on `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` base.

## Architecture tiebreaker (settled from M1 — apply to any override note)

> Option C hybrid, narrowed. `useEntity(id)` is a READER, not authoritative loader. RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through `useAutoSaveSettings → useToolSettings` boundary. `createEntityStore` factory `load` parameter is for store-owned (non-server) entities only. Any RQ→store sync is boundary-internal, NEVER via consumer `useEffect(bootstrapEntity)` bridges. Constraint "useEntity lazy-loads on first mount" was DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise.

## Decision tree — ACT AUTONOMOUSLY (literal plan name, literal key every time)

### A. Chain state shows `complete` (all 5 milestones done) → SUCCESS EXIT
Report **"CHAIN M2-M6 COMPLETE"** loudly. List branches produced (`megaplan/m2-overlay-stack` ... `megaplan/m6-behavior-tests`). Remind human: branches not auto-pushed to GitHub (watchdog scope forbids it). `CronDelete` to stop loop.

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

### C. Active plan state=`critiqued` + next=`override add-note` (gate ESCALATE, known auto-crash)
Megaplan auto crashes trying to invoke `override add-note` as a phase. Apply tiebreaker verdict via `override replan`:
```
megaplan override replan --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "apply tiebreaker verdict" --note "TIEBREAKER VERDICT (Option C hybrid, narrowed, settled from M1): useEntity(id) is a READER not authoritative loader; RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through useAutoSaveSettings->useToolSettings boundary; createEntityStore factory load is for store-owned entities only; any RQ->store sync is boundary-internal NEVER consumer useEffect bridges. Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."
```
If gate ESCALATES a SECOND time on same plan despite the note (flag recurrence), force-proceed:
```
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "Gate ESCALATE recurring despite tiebreaker verdict and executor advisory; Claude review will catch real issues post-execute."
```
Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

### D. Active plan state=`executed` or `critiqued` with gate ESCALATE for reasons OTHER than tiebreaker architecture (FLAG-001/002/003-style concrete spec gaps)
Inspect gate.json for `unresolved_flags`. If flags name specific files/behaviors executor can address (e.g., "file X not in consumer list"), use `override add-note` with an advisory pointing at the concrete fix:
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTE ADVISORY: <specific files and pattern to handle, referencing the flag ID>"
```
Then `override force-proceed` to move forward. This worked on M1c FLAG-001 (useAddToVideoEditor null-safe-hook boundary).

### E. Execute phase returning `result=blocked` repeatedly (codex refusing browser/runtime tasks)
Inject the executor hard rule (if not already in plan metadata from init):
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTOR HARD RULE: browser/runtime-dependent tasks → return status=skipped on FIRST encounter, never status=blocked. Blocked retries waste iteration budget. deferred_human criteria get post-milestone manual verification."
```
This fixed M1b and M1c within 1-2 iterations after injection.

### F. Plan NOT advancing (no history entries in last 15 min, no codex proc, stale .plan.lock)
1. Remove stale lock: `rm /workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/<PLAN>/.plan.lock`
2. Restart chain tmux: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`

### G. Chain tmux session missing entirely (died unexpectedly)
Restart: `mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`. Verify `tmux ls` shows `chain` session. Check `chain.log` for why it died — if it hit `on_escalate: stop_chain` correctly, manually resolve that milestone first (sections C/D/E), then restart chain.

### H. Codex session poisoning (`bwrap: Creating new namespace failed` in exec.log, OR history shows >10 consecutive `result=blocked` with same artifact_hash)
```
rm -rf /root/.codex/sessions/*   # PRESERVE /root/.codex/auth.json
```
Then restart chain (section G). v0.14.6+ auto-detects this but if detection misses manual wipe works.

### I. Disk >90% full
```
find /tmp -name 'tmp*' -type f -mmin +240 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'supervise-*.log' -mtime +1 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'm0-exec.log' -mtime +1 -delete
```

### J. Codex auth lost (`codex login status` not "Logged in using ChatGPT")
STOP and report loud. Only human OAuth recovery. DO NOT re-auth from OPENAI_API_KEY.

### K. Supervisor STREAK with `error: argument --plan: expected one argument`
Variable-expansion bug. Shouldn't happen with megaplan chain (literal plan names), but if it does: look at the failing supervise log, manually relaunch supervisor for the active plan with LITERAL plan name + LITERAL API key hardcoded inline (no `$VAR` inside nested `bash -c '...'`).

## CONSTRAINTS (firm — violations cause incidents)

- NEVER edit `state.json` directly — use `megaplan override ...` commands
- NEVER push to remotes from container — branches are push-by-human-only
- NEVER re-auth codex from OPENAI_API_KEY env var
- NEVER delete `/root/.codex/auth.json`
- ALWAYS use literal plan names + literal API key in relaunch commands (past bug: `$PLAN` expanded empty in nested quoting)
- ALWAYS preserve uncommitted `.megaplan/plans/*` dirs during git operations
- Force-proceed is OK when: (1) gate ESCALATE recurring despite replan-with-verdict; (2) executor advisory note addresses the specific concrete flag; (3) 2+ rework cycles exhausted on same review feedback. NOT OK when: (1) first iteration with substantive gate flags that haven't been addressed; (2) you haven't inspected gate.json rationale.

## Report format (under 250 words)

(1) Chain status: milestone X of 5 (M2/M3/M4/M5/M6), current plan, state, iter.
(2) Progress since last fire: new phases completed, milestone transitions, rework cycles, new execute batches (count).
(3) Actions taken — list each with exact command run (literal names).
(4) Red flags that auto-resolved vs. still concerning.
(5) ETA to chain completion (remaining milestones × observed pace).

If healthy + advancing: one-line `chain healthy, milestone=<M?> plan=<name> state=<X> iter=<N> advancing`.

If you acted: describe the decision-tree branch taken and the command run.

The human does not need to be consulted for any branch A-I. Only J (codex auth lost) and ambiguous force-proceed cases require escalation.

- M1a settings-store rollout (`useAutoSaveSettings` over factory)
- M1b selection store (4 contexts → `selectionStore.ts`)
- M1c timeline store (3 contexts → `timelineStore.ts`)
- `fix: backfill defaults in createEntityStore seed` — prevents partial DB rows surfacing undefined fields

**Human verified in browser**: render counts dropped 15-20 → 1 on lightbox open; LightboxShell 31 → 1; SortableRow 0 renders during clip drag. Motivating bugs effectively dead.

**In flight — YOUR JOB TO DRIVE**: `megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh` running M2 → M3 → M4 → M5 → M6 autonomously on `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` base.

## Architecture tiebreaker (settled from M1 — apply to any override note)

> Option C hybrid, narrowed. `useEntity(id)` is a READER, not authoritative loader. RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through `useAutoSaveSettings → useToolSettings` boundary. `createEntityStore` factory `load` parameter is for store-owned (non-server) entities only. Any RQ→store sync is boundary-internal, NEVER via consumer `useEffect(bootstrapEntity)` bridges. Constraint "useEntity lazy-loads on first mount" was DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise.

## Decision tree — ACT AUTONOMOUSLY (literal plan name, literal key every time)

### A. Chain state shows `complete` (all 5 milestones done) → SUCCESS EXIT
Report **"CHAIN M2-M6 COMPLETE"** loudly. List branches produced (`megaplan/m2-overlay-stack` ... `megaplan/m6-behavior-tests`). Remind human: branches not auto-pushed to GitHub (watchdog scope forbids it). `CronDelete` to stop loop.

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

### C. Active plan state=`critiqued` + next=`override add-note` (gate ESCALATE, known auto-crash)
Megaplan auto crashes trying to invoke `override add-note` as a phase. Apply tiebreaker verdict via `override replan`:
```
megaplan override replan --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "apply tiebreaker verdict" --note "TIEBREAKER VERDICT (Option C hybrid, narrowed, settled from M1): useEntity(id) is a READER not authoritative loader; RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through useAutoSaveSettings->useToolSettings boundary; createEntityStore factory load is for store-owned entities only; any RQ->store sync is boundary-internal NEVER consumer useEffect bridges. Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."
```
If gate ESCALATES a SECOND time on same plan despite the note (flag recurrence), force-proceed:
```
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "Gate ESCALATE recurring despite tiebreaker verdict and executor advisory; Claude review will catch real issues post-execute."
```
Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

### D. Active plan state=`executed` or `critiqued` with gate ESCALATE for reasons OTHER than tiebreaker architecture (FLAG-001/002/003-style concrete spec gaps)
Inspect gate.json for `unresolved_flags`. If flags name specific files/behaviors executor can address (e.g., "file X not in consumer list"), use `override add-note` with an advisory pointing at the concrete fix:
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTE ADVISORY: <specific files and pattern to handle, referencing the flag ID>"
```
Then `override force-proceed` to move forward. This worked on M1c FLAG-001 (useAddToVideoEditor null-safe-hook boundary).

### E. Execute phase returning `result=blocked` repeatedly (codex refusing browser/runtime tasks)
Inject the executor hard rule (if not already in plan metadata from init):
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTOR HARD RULE: browser/runtime-dependent tasks → return status=skipped on FIRST encounter, never status=blocked. Blocked retries waste iteration budget. deferred_human criteria get post-milestone manual verification."
```
This fixed M1b and M1c within 1-2 iterations after injection.

### F. Plan NOT advancing (no history entries in last 15 min, no codex proc, stale .plan.lock)
1. Remove stale lock: `rm /workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/<PLAN>/.plan.lock`
2. Restart chain tmux: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`

### G. Chain tmux session missing entirely (died unexpectedly)
Restart: `mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`. Verify `tmux ls` shows `chain` session. Check `chain.log` for why it died — if it hit `on_escalate: stop_chain` correctly, manually resolve that milestone first (sections C/D/E), then restart chain.

### H. Codex session poisoning (`bwrap: Creating new namespace failed` in exec.log, OR history shows >10 consecutive `result=blocked` with same artifact_hash)
```
rm -rf /root/.codex/sessions/*   # PRESERVE /root/.codex/auth.json
```
Then restart chain (section G). v0.14.6+ auto-detects this but if detection misses manual wipe works.

### I. Disk >90% full
```
find /tmp -name 'tmp*' -type f -mmin +240 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'supervise-*.log' -mtime +1 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'm0-exec.log' -mtime +1 -delete
```

### J. Codex auth lost (`codex login status` not "Logged in using ChatGPT")
STOP and report loud. Only human OAuth recovery. DO NOT re-auth from OPENAI_API_KEY.

### K. Supervisor STREAK with `error: argument --plan: expected one argument`
Variable-expansion bug. Shouldn't happen with megaplan chain (literal plan names), but if it does: look at the failing supervise log, manually relaunch supervisor for the active plan with LITERAL plan name + LITERAL API key hardcoded inline (no `$VAR` inside nested `bash -c '...'`).

## CONSTRAINTS (firm — violations cause incidents)

- NEVER edit `state.json` directly — use `megaplan override ...` commands
- NEVER push to remotes from container — branches are push-by-human-only
- NEVER re-auth codex from OPENAI_API_KEY env var
- NEVER delete `/root/.codex/auth.json`
- ALWAYS use literal plan names + literal API key in relaunch commands (past bug: `$PLAN` expanded empty in nested quoting)
- ALWAYS preserve uncommitted `.megaplan/plans/*` dirs during git operations
- Force-proceed is OK when: (1) gate ESCALATE recurring despite replan-with-verdict; (2) executor advisory note addresses the specific concrete flag; (3) 2+ rework cycles exhausted on same review feedback. NOT OK when: (1) first iteration with substantive gate flags that haven't been addressed; (2) you haven't inspected gate.json rationale.

## Report format (under 250 words)

(1) Chain status: milestone X of 5 (M2/M3/M4/M5/M6), current plan, state, iter.
(2) Progress since last fire: new phases completed, milestone transitions, rework cycles, new execute batches (count).
(3) Actions taken — list each with exact command run (literal names).
(4) Red flags that auto-resolved vs. still concerning.
(5) ETA to chain completion (remaining milestones × observed pace).

If healthy + advancing: one-line `chain healthy, milestone=<M?> plan=<name> state=<X> iter=<N> advancing`.

If you acted: describe the decision-tree branch taken and the command run.

The human does not need to be consulted for any branch A-I. Only J (codex auth lost) and ambiguous force-proceed cases require escalation.

- M1b selection store (4 contexts → `selectionStore.ts`)

## Architecture tiebreaker (settled from M1 — apply to any override note)

> Option C hybrid, narrowed. `useEntity(id)` is a READER, not authoritative loader. RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through `useAutoSaveSettings → useToolSettings` boundary. `createEntityStore` factory `load` parameter is for store-owned (non-server) entities only. Any RQ→store sync is boundary-internal, NEVER via consumer `useEffect(bootstrapEntity)` bridges. Constraint "useEntity lazy-loads on first mount" was DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise.

## Decision tree — ACT AUTONOMOUSLY (literal plan name, literal key every time)

### A. Chain state shows `complete` (all 5 milestones done) → SUCCESS EXIT
Report **"CHAIN M2-M6 COMPLETE"** loudly. List branches produced (`megaplan/m2-overlay-stack` ... `megaplan/m6-behavior-tests`). Remind human: branches not auto-pushed to GitHub (watchdog scope forbids it). `CronDelete` to stop loop.

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

### C. Active plan state=`critiqued` + next=`override add-note` (gate ESCALATE, known auto-crash)
Megaplan auto crashes trying to invoke `override add-note` as a phase. Apply tiebreaker verdict via `override replan`:
```
megaplan override replan --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "apply tiebreaker verdict" --note "TIEBREAKER VERDICT (Option C hybrid, narrowed, settled from M1): useEntity(id) is a READER not authoritative loader; RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through useAutoSaveSettings->useToolSettings boundary; createEntityStore factory load is for store-owned entities only; any RQ->store sync is boundary-internal NEVER consumer useEffect bridges. Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."
```
If gate ESCALATES a SECOND time on same plan despite the note (flag recurrence), force-proceed:
```
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "Gate ESCALATE recurring despite tiebreaker verdict and executor advisory; Claude review will catch real issues post-execute."
```
Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

### D. Active plan state=`executed` or `critiqued` with gate ESCALATE for reasons OTHER than tiebreaker architecture (FLAG-001/002/003-style concrete spec gaps)
Inspect gate.json for `unresolved_flags`. If flags name specific files/behaviors executor can address (e.g., "file X not in consumer list"), use `override add-note` with an advisory pointing at the concrete fix:
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTE ADVISORY: <specific files and pattern to handle, referencing the flag ID>"
```
Then `override force-proceed` to move forward. This worked on M1c FLAG-001 (useAddToVideoEditor null-safe-hook boundary).

### E. Execute phase returning `result=blocked` repeatedly (codex refusing browser/runtime tasks)
Inject the executor hard rule (if not already in plan metadata from init):
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTOR HARD RULE: browser/runtime-dependent tasks → return status=skipped on FIRST encounter, never status=blocked. Blocked retries waste iteration budget. deferred_human criteria get post-milestone manual verification."
```
This fixed M1b and M1c within 1-2 iterations after injection.

### F. Plan NOT advancing (no history entries in last 15 min, no codex proc, stale .plan.lock)
1. Remove stale lock: `rm /workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/<PLAN>/.plan.lock`
2. Restart chain tmux: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`

### G. Chain tmux session missing entirely (died unexpectedly)
Restart: `mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`. Verify `tmux ls` shows `chain` session. Check `chain.log` for why it died — if it hit `on_escalate: stop_chain` correctly, manually resolve that milestone first (sections C/D/E), then restart chain.

### H. Codex session poisoning (`bwrap: Creating new namespace failed` in exec.log, OR history shows >10 consecutive `result=blocked` with same artifact_hash)
```
rm -rf /root/.codex/sessions/*   # PRESERVE /root/.codex/auth.json
```
Then restart chain (section G). v0.14.6+ auto-detects this but if detection misses manual wipe works.

### I. Disk >90% full
```
find /tmp -name 'tmp*' -type f -mmin +240 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'supervise-*.log' -mtime +1 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'm0-exec.log' -mtime +1 -delete
```

### J. Codex auth lost (`codex login status` not "Logged in using ChatGPT")
STOP and report loud. Only human OAuth recovery. DO NOT re-auth from OPENAI_API_KEY.

### K. Supervisor STREAK with `error: argument --plan: expected one argument`
Variable-expansion bug. Shouldn't happen with megaplan chain (literal plan names), but if it does: look at the failing supervise log, manually relaunch supervisor for the active plan with LITERAL plan name + LITERAL API key hardcoded inline (no `$VAR` inside nested `bash -c '...'`).

## CONSTRAINTS (firm — violations cause incidents)

- NEVER edit `state.json` directly — use `megaplan override ...` commands
- NEVER push to remotes from container — branches are push-by-human-only
- NEVER re-auth codex from OPENAI_API_KEY env var
- NEVER delete `/root/.codex/auth.json`
- ALWAYS use literal plan names + literal API key in relaunch commands (past bug: `$PLAN` expanded empty in nested quoting)
- ALWAYS preserve uncommitted `.megaplan/plans/*` dirs during git operations
- Force-proceed is OK when: (1) gate ESCALATE recurring despite replan-with-verdict; (2) executor advisory note addresses the specific concrete flag; (3) 2+ rework cycles exhausted on same review feedback. NOT OK when: (1) first iteration with substantive gate flags that haven't been addressed; (2) you haven't inspected gate.json rationale.

## Report format (under 250 words)

(1) Chain status: milestone X of 5 (M2/M3/M4/M5/M6), current plan, state, iter.
(2) Progress since last fire: new phases completed, milestone transitions, rework cycles, new execute batches (count).
(3) Actions taken — list each with exact command run (literal names).
(4) Red flags that auto-resolved vs. still concerning.
(5) ETA to chain completion (remaining milestones × observed pace).

If healthy + advancing: one-line `chain healthy, milestone=<M?> plan=<name> state=<X> iter=<N> advancing`.

If you acted: describe the decision-tree branch taken and the command run.

The human does not need to be consulted for any branch A-I. Only J (codex auth lost) and ambiguous force-proceed cases require escalation.

- M0 render telemetry baseline
- M1 `createEntityStore` factory + `useJoinClipsSettings` port
- M1a settings-store rollout (`useAutoSaveSettings` over factory)
- M1b selection store (4 contexts → `selectionStore.ts`)
- M1c timeline store (3 contexts → `timelineStore.ts`)
- `fix: backfill defaults in createEntityStore seed` — prevents partial DB rows surfacing undefined fields

**Human verified in browser**: render counts dropped 15-20 → 1 on lightbox open; LightboxShell 31 → 1; SortableRow 0 renders during clip drag. Motivating bugs effectively dead.

**In flight — YOUR JOB TO DRIVE**: `megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh` running M2 → M3 → M4 → M5 → M6 autonomously on `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` base.

**Pending (by design)**: push per-milestone branches to GitHub (human will do post-chain); open PRs (human); M1a dependency audit of `useImageLightboxEnvironment` (nice-to-have, not blocking).

## Architecture tiebreaker (settled from M1 — apply to any override note)

> Option C hybrid, narrowed. `useEntity(id)` is a READER, not authoritative loader. RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through `useAutoSaveSettings → useToolSettings` boundary. `createEntityStore` factory `load` parameter is for store-owned (non-server) entities only. Any RQ→store sync is boundary-internal, NEVER via consumer `useEffect(bootstrapEntity)` bridges. Constraint "useEntity lazy-loads on first mount" was DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise.

## Decision tree — ACT AUTONOMOUSLY (literal plan name, literal key every time)

### A. Chain state shows `complete` (all 5 milestones done) → SUCCESS EXIT
Report **"CHAIN M2-M6 COMPLETE"** loudly. List branches produced (`megaplan/m2-overlay-stack` ... `megaplan/m6-behavior-tests`). Remind human: branches not auto-pushed to GitHub (watchdog scope forbids it). `CronDelete` to stop loop.

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

### C. Active plan state=`critiqued` + next=`override add-note` (gate ESCALATE, known auto-crash)
Megaplan auto crashes trying to invoke `override add-note` as a phase. Apply tiebreaker verdict via `override replan`:
```
megaplan override replan --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "apply tiebreaker verdict" --note "TIEBREAKER VERDICT (Option C hybrid, narrowed, settled from M1): useEntity(id) is a READER not authoritative loader; RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through useAutoSaveSettings->useToolSettings boundary; createEntityStore factory load is for store-owned entities only; any RQ->store sync is boundary-internal NEVER consumer useEffect bridges. Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."
```
If gate ESCALATES a SECOND time on same plan despite the note (flag recurrence), force-proceed:
```
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "Gate ESCALATE recurring despite tiebreaker verdict and executor advisory; Claude review will catch real issues post-execute."
```
Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

### D. Active plan state=`executed` or `critiqued` with gate ESCALATE for reasons OTHER than tiebreaker architecture (FLAG-001/002/003-style concrete spec gaps)
Inspect gate.json for `unresolved_flags`. If flags name specific files/behaviors executor can address (e.g., "file X not in consumer list"), use `override add-note` with an advisory pointing at the concrete fix:
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTE ADVISORY: <specific files and pattern to handle, referencing the flag ID>"
```
Then `override force-proceed` to move forward. This worked on M1c FLAG-001 (useAddToVideoEditor null-safe-hook boundary).

### E. Execute phase returning `result=blocked` repeatedly (codex refusing browser/runtime tasks)
Inject the executor hard rule (if not already in plan metadata from init):
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTOR HARD RULE: browser/runtime-dependent tasks → return status=skipped on FIRST encounter, never status=blocked. Blocked retries waste iteration budget. deferred_human criteria get post-milestone manual verification."
```
This fixed M1b and M1c within 1-2 iterations after injection.

### F. Plan NOT advancing (no history entries in last 15 min, no codex proc, stale .plan.lock)
1. Remove stale lock: `rm /workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/<PLAN>/.plan.lock`
2. Restart chain tmux: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`

### G. Chain tmux session missing entirely (died unexpectedly)
Restart: `mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`. Verify `tmux ls` shows `chain` session. Check `chain.log` for why it died — if it hit `on_escalate: stop_chain` correctly, manually resolve that milestone first (sections C/D/E), then restart chain.

### H. Codex session poisoning (`bwrap: Creating new namespace failed` in exec.log, OR history shows >10 consecutive `result=blocked` with same artifact_hash)
```
rm -rf /root/.codex/sessions/*   # PRESERVE /root/.codex/auth.json
```
Then restart chain (section G). v0.14.6+ auto-detects this but if detection misses manual wipe works.

### I. Disk >90% full
```
find /tmp -name 'tmp*' -type f -mmin +240 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'supervise-*.log' -mtime +1 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'm0-exec.log' -mtime +1 -delete
```

### J. Codex auth lost (`codex login status` not "Logged in using ChatGPT")
STOP and report loud. Only human OAuth recovery. DO NOT re-auth from OPENAI_API_KEY.

### K. Supervisor STREAK with `error: argument --plan: expected one argument`
Variable-expansion bug. Shouldn't happen with megaplan chain (literal plan names), but if it does: look at the failing supervise log, manually relaunch supervisor for the active plan with LITERAL plan name + LITERAL API key hardcoded inline (no `$VAR` inside nested `bash -c '...'`).

## CONSTRAINTS (firm — violations cause incidents)

- NEVER edit `state.json` directly — use `megaplan override ...` commands
- NEVER push to remotes from container — branches are push-by-human-only
- NEVER re-auth codex from OPENAI_API_KEY env var
- NEVER delete `/root/.codex/auth.json`
- ALWAYS use literal plan names + literal API key in relaunch commands (past bug: `$PLAN` expanded empty in nested quoting)
- ALWAYS preserve uncommitted `.megaplan/plans/*` dirs during git operations
- Force-proceed is OK when: (1) gate ESCALATE recurring despite replan-with-verdict; (2) executor advisory note addresses the specific concrete flag; (3) 2+ rework cycles exhausted on same review feedback. NOT OK when: (1) first iteration with substantive gate flags that haven't been addressed; (2) you haven't inspected gate.json rationale.

## Report format (under 250 words)

(1) Chain status: milestone X of 5 (M2/M3/M4/M5/M6), current plan, state, iter.
(2) Progress since last fire: new phases completed, milestone transitions, rework cycles, new execute batches (count).
(3) Actions taken — list each with exact command run (literal names).
(4) Red flags that auto-resolved vs. still concerning.
(5) ETA to chain completion (remaining milestones × observed pace).

If healthy + advancing: one-line `chain healthy, milestone=<M?> plan=<name> state=<X> iter=<N> advancing`.

If you acted: describe the decision-tree branch taken and the command run.

The human does not need to be consulted for any branch A-I. Only J (codex auth lost) and ambiguous force-proceed cases require escalation.

## What we're doing (big picture)

**Completed (on GitHub branch `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores`, commit `77bbb9340`)**:
- M0 render telemetry baseline
- M1 `createEntityStore` factory + `useJoinClipsSettings` port
- M1a settings-store rollout (`useAutoSaveSettings` over factory)
- M1b selection store (4 contexts → `selectionStore.ts`)
- M1c timeline store (3 contexts → `timelineStore.ts`)
- `fix: backfill defaults in createEntityStore seed` — prevents partial DB rows surfacing undefined fields

**Human verified in browser**: render counts dropped 15-20 → 1 on lightbox open; LightboxShell 31 → 1; SortableRow 0 renders during clip drag. Motivating bugs effectively dead.

**In flight — YOUR JOB TO DRIVE**: `megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh` running M2 → M3 → M4 → M5 → M6 autonomously on `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` base.

**Pending (by design)**: push per-milestone branches to GitHub (human will do post-chain); open PRs (human); M1a dependency audit of `useImageLightboxEnvironment` (nice-to-have, not blocking).

## Architecture tiebreaker (settled from M1 — apply to any override note)

> Option C hybrid, narrowed. `useEntity(id)` is a READER, not authoritative loader. RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through `useAutoSaveSettings → useToolSettings` boundary. `createEntityStore` factory `load` parameter is for store-owned (non-server) entities only. Any RQ→store sync is boundary-internal, NEVER via consumer `useEffect(bootstrapEntity)` bridges. Constraint "useEntity lazy-loads on first mount" was DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise.

## Decision tree — ACT AUTONOMOUSLY (literal plan name, literal key every time)

### A. Chain state shows `complete` (all 5 milestones done) → SUCCESS EXIT
Report **"CHAIN M2-M6 COMPLETE"** loudly. List branches produced (`megaplan/m2-overlay-stack` ... `megaplan/m6-behavior-tests`). Remind human: branches not auto-pushed to GitHub (watchdog scope forbids it). `CronDelete` to stop loop.

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

### C. Active plan state=`critiqued` + next=`override add-note` (gate ESCALATE, known auto-crash)
Megaplan auto crashes trying to invoke `override add-note` as a phase. Apply tiebreaker verdict via `override replan`:
```
megaplan override replan --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "apply tiebreaker verdict" --note "TIEBREAKER VERDICT (Option C hybrid, narrowed, settled from M1): useEntity(id) is a READER not authoritative loader; RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through useAutoSaveSettings->useToolSettings boundary; createEntityStore factory load is for store-owned entities only; any RQ->store sync is boundary-internal NEVER consumer useEffect bridges. Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."
```
If gate ESCALATES a SECOND time on same plan despite the note (flag recurrence), force-proceed:
```
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "Gate ESCALATE recurring despite tiebreaker verdict and executor advisory; Claude review will catch real issues post-execute."
```
Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

### D. Active plan state=`executed` or `critiqued` with gate ESCALATE for reasons OTHER than tiebreaker architecture (FLAG-001/002/003-style concrete spec gaps)
Inspect gate.json for `unresolved_flags`. If flags name specific files/behaviors executor can address (e.g., "file X not in consumer list"), use `override add-note` with an advisory pointing at the concrete fix:
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTE ADVISORY: <specific files and pattern to handle, referencing the flag ID>"
```
Then `override force-proceed` to move forward. This worked on M1c FLAG-001 (useAddToVideoEditor null-safe-hook boundary).

### E. Execute phase returning `result=blocked` repeatedly (codex refusing browser/runtime tasks)
Inject the executor hard rule (if not already in plan metadata from init):
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTOR HARD RULE: browser/runtime-dependent tasks → return status=skipped on FIRST encounter, never status=blocked. Blocked retries waste iteration budget. deferred_human criteria get post-milestone manual verification."
```
This fixed M1b and M1c within 1-2 iterations after injection.

### F. Plan NOT advancing (no history entries in last 15 min, no codex proc, stale .plan.lock)
1. Remove stale lock: `rm /workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/<PLAN>/.plan.lock`
2. Restart chain tmux: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`

### G. Chain tmux session missing entirely (died unexpectedly)
Restart: `mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`. Verify `tmux ls` shows `chain` session. Check `chain.log` for why it died — if it hit `on_escalate: stop_chain` correctly, manually resolve that milestone first (sections C/D/E), then restart chain.

### H. Codex session poisoning (`bwrap: Creating new namespace failed` in exec.log, OR history shows >10 consecutive `result=blocked` with same artifact_hash)
```
rm -rf /root/.codex/sessions/*   # PRESERVE /root/.codex/auth.json
```
Then restart chain (section G). v0.14.6+ auto-detects this but if detection misses manual wipe works.

### I. Disk >90% full
```
find /tmp -name 'tmp*' -type f -mmin +240 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'supervise-*.log' -mtime +1 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'm0-exec.log' -mtime +1 -delete
```

### J. Codex auth lost (`codex login status` not "Logged in using ChatGPT")
STOP and report loud. Only human OAuth recovery. DO NOT re-auth from OPENAI_API_KEY.

### K. Supervisor STREAK with `error: argument --plan: expected one argument`
Variable-expansion bug. Shouldn't happen with megaplan chain (literal plan names), but if it does: look at the failing supervise log, manually relaunch supervisor for the active plan with LITERAL plan name + LITERAL API key hardcoded inline (no `$VAR` inside nested `bash -c '...'`).

## CONSTRAINTS (firm — violations cause incidents)

- NEVER edit `state.json` directly — use `megaplan override ...` commands
- NEVER push to remotes from container — branches are push-by-human-only
- NEVER re-auth codex from OPENAI_API_KEY env var
- NEVER delete `/root/.codex/auth.json`
- ALWAYS use literal plan names + literal API key in relaunch commands (past bug: `$PLAN` expanded empty in nested quoting)
- ALWAYS preserve uncommitted `.megaplan/plans/*` dirs during git operations
- Force-proceed is OK when: (1) gate ESCALATE recurring despite replan-with-verdict; (2) executor advisory note addresses the specific concrete flag; (3) 2+ rework cycles exhausted on same review feedback. NOT OK when: (1) first iteration with substantive gate flags that haven't been addressed; (2) you haven't inspected gate.json rationale.

## Report format (under 250 words)

(1) Chain status: milestone X of 5 (M2/M3/M4/M5/M6), current plan, state, iter.
(2) Progress since last fire: new phases completed, milestone transitions, rework cycles, new execute batches (count).
(3) Actions taken — list each with exact command run (literal names).
(4) Red flags that auto-resolved vs. still concerning.
(5) ETA to chain completion (remaining milestones × observed pace).

If healthy + advancing: one-line `chain healthy, milestone=<M?> plan=<name> state=<X> iter=<N> advancing`.

If you acted: describe the decision-tree branch taken and the command run.

The human does not need to be consulted for any branch A-I. Only J (codex auth lost) and ambiguous force-proceed cases require escalation.

## Decision tree — ACT AUTONOMOUSLY (literal plan name, literal key every time)

### A. Chain state shows `complete` (all 5 milestones done) → SUCCESS EXIT
Report **"CHAIN M2-M6 COMPLETE"** loudly. List branches produced (`megaplan/m2-overlay-stack` ... `megaplan/m6-behavior-tests`). Remind human: branches not auto-pushed to GitHub (watchdog scope forbids it). `CronDelete` to stop loop.

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."

Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

- NEVER delete `/root/.codex/auth.json`
- ALWAYS use literal plan names + literal API key in relaunch commands (past bug: `$PLAN` expanded empty in nested quoting)
- ALWAYS preserve uncommitted `.megaplan/plans/*` dirs during git operations
- Force-proceed is OK when: (1) gate ESCALATE recurring despite replan-with-verdict; (2) executor advisory note addresses the specific concrete flag; (3) 2+ rework cycles exhausted on same review feedback. NOT OK when: (1) first iteration with substantive gate flags that haven't been addressed; (2) you haven't inspected gate.json rationale.

## Report format (under 250 words)

(1) Chain status: milestone X of 5 (M2/M3/M4/M5/M6), current plan, state, iter.
(2) Progress since last fire: new phases completed, milestone transitions, rework cycles, new execute batches (count).
(3) Actions taken — list each with exact command run (literal names).
(4) Red flags that auto-resolved vs. still concerning.
(5) ETA to chain completion (remaining milestones × observed pace).

If healthy + advancing: one-line `chain healthy, milestone=<M?> plan=<name> state=<X> iter=<N> advancing`.

If you acted: describe the decision-tree branch taken and the command run.

The human does not need to be consulted for any branch A-I. Only J (codex auth lost) and ambiguous force-proceed cases require escalation.

## The root cause

**Both rework items are trivial code-level tasks** — not browser/runtime work. I was wrong about that earlier:

- **T5**: Update `docs/state_management_context_audit.md` to be a complete per-declaration inventory (some split contexts like `ImageGenerationFormContext` / `LightboxStateContext` are summarized as single entries when they should be itemized).
- **T7**: Extend `scripts/quality/check-fat-contexts.mjs` regex to match `React.createContext(...)` (currently only matches bare `createContext(...)`).

These are small mechanical edits. Codex absolutely can do them. But it's returning `blocked` on every retry.

**The true root**: the review demands *asymptotic perfection* on tasks where codex has already done its best, and megaplan has no "good enough, ship it" exit.

First execute produced a reasonable doc and a reasonable regex. Review said "still incomplete" / "still doesn't cover all forms." Codex's subsequent attempts produce essentially the same output — it has no new information about what specifically the reviewer wants *added*. So codex returns `blocked` to signal "I've done what I can." Megaplan interprets `blocked` as "retry" and re-issues the same prompt. Loop. Stall.

Compounding:
1. My EXECUTOR HARD RULE advisory was about browser/runtime items — irrelevant to these code-level tasks. So it had no effect.
2. `max_review_rework_cycles: 3` never fires because the counter increments on review passes, not on execute blocks.
3. `codex exec resume` with a fixed session UUID — if that session cached a "can't improve further" response, every resume returns it.
4. `force-proceed` is rejected from state=`finalized`.

**The exit**: just do the two edits manually. They're 15 lines total. Then either re-run review (which should pass) or override-step to push the plan to `done`. Want me to do that?

So codex *says* it edited the audit doc, but megaplan runs `git status` to verify and the file isn't in the diff — meaning either the edit produced no actual diff (codex's "update" wrote content identical to what was already there) or codex fabricated the claim. Megaplan marks the whole batch `blocked` on that mismatch. Retry loop never recovers because `codex exec resume <session-id>` keeps reusing the same poisoned session, which produces the same non-edit.

**The upstream bug (the one the user already smelled)**: the chain isn't committing between milestones. Megaplan's execution audit assumes each milestone starts from a clean working tree so it can match codex's "files I changed" claim against `git status`. Because M2 + M3 never got committed:

1. The working tree is polluted with 166 unrelated files — flagged as "unclaimed changes" noise.
2. When codex's T5 edit happens to produce no diff (file already has matching content from earlier cruft), the audit can't tell the edit was a no-op vs. a lie.
3. Both conditions together → `blocked`.

**Bugs that need fixing (in order of leverage)**:

1. **Chain spec has `branch:` per milestone but no commit hook.** M2 and M3 reached `done` without anything being committed or branch-created. This is the prime bug — it violates the invariant megaplan's audit relies on. Either megaplan should auto-commit at milestone end, or the spec needs a `post_milestone: git commit -am "..."` hook.

2. **`codex exec resume` with a fixed session UUID means session poisoning.** When a batch returns `blocked`, the next execute shouldn't `resume` — it should start a new session with fresh context. The cron's section H already anticipates this as "session poisoning."

3. **The audit's `blocked` verdict has no remediation path.** When `files_claimed` doesn't match `files_in_diff`, the fix isn't "retry same prompt" — it's either accept the no-op or reprompt codex with the specific mismatch. Current behavior is just infinite retry.

**The fastest unblock for right now**: commit the accumulated M2+M3 work to its own branch, then continue M4 from that clean base. That addresses #1 directly and makes the audit findings meaningful again. Want me to do that, or dig into fixing the chain spec first?

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```

**Real root cause found in the batch's own deviation list:**

> "docs/state_management_context_audit.md is matched by `.gitignore` (`*.md`), so its update exists on disk for this workspace but does not appear in `git status`."

**The repo has `*.md` in `.gitignore`.** Codex edits the file, it's written to disk, but megaplan's audit runs `git status` to verify and can never see it. Infinite blocked loop. My earlier commit didn't help because the problem isn't cross-milestone cruft — it's that this specific file can't ever show up in `git status` no matter what codex does.

Fix: add a `.gitignore` exception so megaplan's audit can see the file.

## Decision tree — ACT AUTONOMOUSLY (literal plan name, literal key every time)

### A. Chain state shows `complete` (all 5 milestones done) → SUCCESS EXIT
Report **"CHAIN M2-M6 COMPLETE"** loudly. List branches produced (`megaplan/m2-overlay-stack` ... `megaplan/m6-behavior-tests`). Remind human: branches not auto-pushed to GitHub (watchdog scope forbids it). `CronDelete` to stop loop.

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

### C. Active plan state=`critiqued` + next=`override add-note` (gate ESCALATE, known auto-crash)
Megaplan auto crashes trying to invoke `override add-note` as a phase. Apply tiebreaker verdict via `override replan`:
```
megaplan override replan --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "apply tiebreaker verdict" --note "TIEBREAKER VERDICT (Option C hybrid, narrowed, settled from M1): useEntity(id) is a READER not authoritative loader; RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through useAutoSaveSettings->useToolSettings boundary; createEntityStore factory load is for store-owned entities only; any RQ->store sync is boundary-internal NEVER consumer useEffect bridges. Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."
```
If gate ESCALATES a SECOND time on same plan despite the note (flag recurrence), force-proceed:
```
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "Gate ESCALATE recurring despite tiebreaker verdict and executor advisory; Claude review will catch real issues post-execute."
```
Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

### D. Active plan state=`executed` or `critiqued` with gate ESCALATE for reasons OTHER than tiebreaker architecture (FLAG-001/002/003-style concrete spec gaps)
Inspect gate.json for `unresolved_flags`. If flags name specific files/behaviors executor can address (e.g., "file X not in consumer list"), use `override add-note` with an advisory pointing at the concrete fix:
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTE ADVISORY: <specific files and pattern to handle, referencing the flag ID>"
```
Then `override force-proceed` to move forward. This worked on M1c FLAG-001 (useAddToVideoEditor null-safe-hook boundary).

### E. Execute phase returning `result=blocked` repeatedly (codex refusing browser/runtime tasks)
Inject the executor hard rule (if not already in plan metadata from init):
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTOR HARD RULE: browser/runtime-dependent tasks → return status=skipped on FIRST encounter, never status=blocked. Blocked retries waste iteration budget. deferred_human criteria get post-milestone manual verification."
```
This fixed M1b and M1c within 1-2 iterations after injection.

### F. Plan NOT advancing (no history entries in last 15 min, no codex proc, stale .plan.lock)
1. Remove stale lock: `rm /workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/<PLAN>/.plan.lock`
2. Restart chain tmux: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`

### G. Chain tmux session missing entirely (died unexpectedly)
Restart: `mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`. Verify `tmux ls` shows `chain` session. Check `chain.log` for why it died — if it hit `on_escalate: stop_chain` correctly, manually resolve that milestone first (sections C/D/E), then restart chain.

### H. Codex session poisoning (`bwrap: Creating new namespace failed` in exec.log, OR history shows >10 consecutive `result=blocked` with same artifact_hash)
```
rm -rf /root/.codex/sessions/*   # PRESERVE /root/.codex/auth.json
```
Then restart chain (section G). v0.14.6+ auto-detects this but if detection misses manual wipe works.

### I. Disk >90% full
```
find /tmp -name 'tmp*' -type f -mmin +240 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'supervise-*.log' -mtime +1 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'm0-exec.log' -mtime +1 -delete
```

### J. Codex auth lost (`codex login status` not "Logged in using ChatGPT")
STOP and report loud. Only human OAuth recovery. DO NOT re-auth from OPENAI_API_KEY.

### K. Supervisor STREAK with `error: argument --plan: expected one argument`
Variable-expansion bug. Shouldn't happen with megaplan chain (literal plan names), but if it does: look at the failing supervise log, manually relaunch supervisor for the active plan with LITERAL plan name + LITERAL API key hardcoded inline (no `$VAR` inside nested `bash -c '...'`).

## CONSTRAINTS (firm — violations cause incidents)

- NEVER edit `state.json` directly — use `megaplan override ...` commands
- NEVER push to remotes from container — branches are push-by-human-only
- NEVER re-auth codex from OPENAI_API_KEY env var
- NEVER delete `/root/.codex/auth.json`
- ALWAYS use literal plan names + literal API key in relaunch commands (past bug: `$PLAN` expanded empty in nested quoting)
- ALWAYS preserve uncommitted `.megaplan/plans/*` dirs during git operations
- Force-proceed is OK when: (1) gate ESCALATE recurring despite replan-with-verdict; (2) executor advisory note addresses the specific concrete flag; (3) 2+ rework cycles exhausted on same review feedback. NOT OK when: (1) first iteration with substantive gate flags that haven't been addressed; (2) you haven't inspected gate.json rationale.

The human does not need to be consulted for any branch A-I. Only J (codex auth lost) and ambiguous force-proceed cases require escalation.

## Architecture tiebreaker (settled from M1 — apply to any override note)

> Option C hybrid, narrowed. `useEntity(id)` is a READER, not authoritative loader. RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through `useAutoSaveSettings → useToolSettings` boundary. `createEntityStore` factory `load` parameter is for store-owned (non-server) entities only. Any RQ→store sync is boundary-internal, NEVER via consumer `useEffect(bootstrapEntity)` bridges. Constraint "useEntity lazy-loads on first mount" was DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise.
