## Decision tree — ACT AUTONOMOUSLY (literal plan name, literal key every time)

### A. Chain state shows `complete` (all 5 milestones done) → SUCCESS EXIT
Report **"CHAIN M2-M6 COMPLETE"** loudly. List branches produced (`megaplan/m2-overlay-stack` ... `megaplan/m6-behavior-tests`). Remind human: branches not auto-pushed to GitHub (watchdog scope forbids it). `CronDelete` to stop loop.

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

### C. Active plan state=`critiqued` + next=`override add-note` (gate ESCALATE, known auto-crash)
Megaplan auto crashes trying to invoke `override add-note` as a phase. Apply tiebreaker verdict via `override replan`:
```
megaplan override replan --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "apply tiebreaker verdict" --note "TIEBREAKER VERDICT (Option C hybrid, narrowed, settled from M1): useEntity(id) is a READER not authoritative loader; RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through useAutoSaveSettings->useToolSettings boundary; createEntityStore factory load is for store-owned entities only; any RQ->store sync is boundary-internal NEVER consumer useEffect bridges. Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."
```
If gate ESCALATES a SECOND time on same plan despite the note (flag recurrence), force-proceed:
```
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "Gate ESCALATE recurring despite tiebreaker verdict and executor advisory; Claude review will catch real issues post-execute."
```
Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

### D. Active plan state=`executed` or `critiqued` with gate ESCALATE for reasons OTHER than tiebreaker architecture (FLAG-001/002/003-style concrete spec gaps)
Inspect gate.json for `unresolved_flags`. If flags name specific files/behaviors executor can address (e.g., "file X not in consumer list"), use `override add-note` with an advisory pointing at the concrete fix:
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTE ADVISORY: <specific files and pattern to handle, referencing the flag ID>"
```
Then `override force-proceed` to move forward. This worked on M1c FLAG-001 (useAddToVideoEditor null-safe-hook boundary).

### E. Execute phase returning `result=blocked` repeatedly (codex refusing browser/runtime tasks)
Inject the executor hard rule (if not already in plan metadata from init):
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTOR HARD RULE: browser/runtime-dependent tasks → return status=skipped on FIRST encounter, never status=blocked. Blocked retries waste iteration budget. deferred_human criteria get post-milestone manual verification."
```
This fixed M1b and M1c within 1-2 iterations after injection.

### F. Plan NOT advancing (no history entries in last 15 min, no codex proc, stale .plan.lock)
1. Remove stale lock: `rm /workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/<PLAN>/.plan.lock`
2. Restart chain tmux: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`

### G. Chain tmux session missing entirely (died unexpectedly)
Restart: `mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`. Verify `tmux ls` shows `chain` session. Check `chain.log` for why it died — if it hit `on_escalate: stop_chain` correctly, manually resolve that milestone first (sections C/D/E), then restart chain.

### H. Codex session poisoning (`bwrap: Creating new namespace failed` in exec.log, OR history shows >10 consecutive `result=blocked` with same artifact_hash)
```
rm -rf /root/.codex/sessions/*   # PRESERVE /root/.codex/auth.json
```
Then restart chain (section G). v0.14.6+ auto-detects this but if detection misses manual wipe works.

### J. Codex auth lost (`codex login status` not "Logged in using ChatGPT")
STOP and report loud. Only human OAuth recovery. DO NOT re-auth from OPENAI_API_KEY.

### K. Supervisor STREAK with `error: argument --plan: expected one argument`
Variable-expansion bug. Shouldn't happen with megaplan chain (literal plan names), but if it does: look at the failing supervise log, manually relaunch supervisor for the active plan with LITERAL plan name + LITERAL API key hardcoded inline (no `$VAR` inside nested `bash -c '...'`).

## CONSTRAINTS (firm — violations cause incidents)

- NEVER edit `state.json` directly — use `megaplan override ...` commands
- NEVER push to remotes from container — branches are push-by-human-only
- NEVER re-auth codex from OPENAI_API_KEY env var
- NEVER delete `/root/.codex/auth.json`
- ALWAYS use literal plan names + literal API key in relaunch commands (past bug: `$PLAN` expanded empty in nested quoting)
- ALWAYS preserve uncommitted `.megaplan/plans/*` dirs during git operations
- Force-proceed is OK when: (1) gate ESCALATE recurring despite replan-with-verdict; (2) executor advisory note addresses the specific concrete flag; (3) 2+ rework cycles exhausted on same review feedback. NOT OK when: (1) first iteration with substantive gate flags that haven't been addressed; (2) you haven't inspected gate.json rationale.

## Report format (under 250 words)

(1) Chain status: milestone X of 5 (M2/M3/M4/M5/M6), current plan, state, iter.
(2) Progress since last fire: new phases completed, milestone transitions, rework cycles, new execute batches (count).
(3) Actions taken — list each with exact command run (literal names).
(4) Red flags that auto-resolved vs. still concerning.
(5) ETA to chain completion (remaining milestones × observed pace).

If healthy + advancing: one-line `chain healthy, milestone=<M?> plan=<name> state=<X> iter=<N> advancing`.

If you acted: describe the decision-tree branch taken and the command run.

The human does not need to be consulted for any branch A-I. Only J (codex auth lost) and ambiguous force-proceed cases require escalation.

> Option C hybrid, narrowed. `useEntity(id)` is a READER, not authoritative loader. ## Decision tree — ACT AUTONOMOUSLY (literal plan name, literal key every time)

### A. Chain state shows `complete` (all 5 milestones done) → SUCCESS EXIT
Report **"CHAIN M2-M6 COMPLETE"** loudly. List branches produced (`megaplan/m2-overlay-stack` ... `megaplan/m6-behavior-tests`). Remind human: branches not auto-pushed to GitHub (watchdog scope forbids it). `CronDelete` to stop loop.

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

### C. Active plan state=`critiqued` + next=`override add-note` (gate ESCALATE, known auto-crash)
Megaplan auto crashes trying to invoke `override add-note` as a phase. Apply tiebreaker verdict via `override replan`:
```
megaplan override replan --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "apply tiebreaker verdict" --note "TIEBREAKER VERDICT (Option C hybrid, narrowed, settled from M1): useEntity(id) is a READER not authoritative loader; RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through useAutoSaveSettings->useToolSettings boundary; createEntityStore factory load is for store-owned entities only; any RQ->store sync is boundary-internal NEVER consumer useEffect bridges. Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."
```
If gate ESCALATES a SECOND time on same plan despite the note (flag recurrence), force-proceed:
```
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "Gate ESCALATE recurring despite tiebreaker verdict and executor advisory; Claude review will catch real issues post-execute."
```
Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

### D. Active plan state=`executed` or `critiqued` with gate ESCALATE for reasons OTHER than tiebreaker architecture (FLAG-001/002/003-style concrete spec gaps)
Inspect gate.json for `unresolved_flags`. If flags name specific files/behaviors executor can address (e.g., "file X not in consumer list"), use `override add-note` with an advisory pointing at the concrete fix:
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTE ADVISORY: <specific files and pattern to handle, referencing the flag ID>"
```
Then `override force-proceed` to move forward. This worked on M1c FLAG-001 (useAddToVideoEditor null-safe-hook boundary).

### E. Execute phase returning `result=blocked` repeatedly (codex refusing browser/runtime tasks)
Inject the executor hard rule (if not already in plan metadata from init):
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTOR HARD RULE: browser/runtime-dependent tasks → return status=skipped on FIRST encounter, never status=blocked. Blocked retries waste iteration budget. deferred_human criteria get post-milestone manual verification."
```
This fixed M1b and M1c within 1-2 iterations after injection.

### F. Plan NOT advancing (no history entries in last 15 min, no codex proc, stale .plan.lock)
1. Remove stale lock: `rm /workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/<PLAN>/.plan.lock`
2. Restart chain tmux: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`

### G. Chain tmux session missing entirely (died unexpectedly)
Restart: `mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`. Verify `tmux ls` shows `chain` session. Check `chain.log` for why it died — if it hit `on_escalate: stop_chain` correctly, manually resolve that milestone first (sections C/D/E), then restart chain.

### H. Codex session poisoning (`bwrap: Creating new namespace failed` in exec.log, OR history shows >10 consecutive `result=blocked` with same artifact_hash)
```
rm -rf /root/.codex/sessions/*   # PRESERVE /root/.codex/auth.json
```
Then restart chain (section G). v0.14.6+ auto-detects this but if detection misses manual wipe works.

### I. Disk >90% full
```
find /tmp -name 'tmp*' -type f -mmin +240 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'supervise-*.log' -mtime +1 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'm0-exec.log' -mtime +1 -delete
```

### J. Codex auth lost (`codex login status` not "Logged in using ChatGPT")
STOP and report loud. Only human OAuth recovery. DO NOT re-auth from OPENAI_API_KEY.

### K. Supervisor STREAK with `error: argument --plan: expected one argument`
Variable-expansion bug. Shouldn't happen with megaplan chain (literal plan names), but if it does: look at the failing supervise log, manually relaunch supervisor for the active plan with LITERAL plan name + LITERAL API key hardcoded inline (no `$VAR` inside nested `bash -c '...'`).

## CONSTRAINTS (firm — violations cause incidents)

- NEVER edit `state.json` directly — use `megaplan override ...` commands
- NEVER push to remotes from container — branches are push-by-human-only
- NEVER re-auth codex from OPENAI_API_KEY env var
- NEVER delete `/root/.codex/auth.json`
- ALWAYS use literal plan names + literal API key in relaunch commands (past bug: `$PLAN` expanded empty in nested quoting)
- ALWAYS preserve uncommitted `.megaplan/plans/*` dirs during git operations
- Force-proceed is OK when: (1) gate ESCALATE recurring despite replan-with-verdict; (2) executor advisory note addresses the specific concrete flag; (3) 2+ rework cycles exhausted on same review feedback. NOT OK when: (1) first iteration with substantive gate flags that haven't been addressed; (2) you haven't inspected gate.json rationale.

If you acted: describe the decision-tree branch taken and the command run.

The human does not need to be consulted for any branch A-I. Only J (codex auth lost) and ambiguous force-proceed cases require escalation.

## Decision tree — ACT AUTONOMOUSLY (literal plan name, literal key every time)

### A. Chain state shows `complete` (all 5 milestones done) → SUCCESS EXIT
Report **"CHAIN M2-M6 COMPLETE"** loudly. List branches produced (`megaplan/m2-overlay-stack` ... `megaplan/m6-behavior-tests`). Remind human: branches not auto-pushed to GitHub (watchdog scope forbids it). `CronDelete` to stop loop.

### B. Active plan state=`awaiting_human_verify` → AUTO-VERIFY IMMEDIATELY
Claude-review approval supersedes per-criterion sign-off. Run:
```
cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

### C. Active plan state=`critiqued` + next=`override add-note` (gate ESCALATE, known auto-crash)
Megaplan auto crashes trying to invoke `override add-note` as a phase. Apply tiebreaker verdict via `override replan`:
```
megaplan override replan --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "apply tiebreaker verdict" --note "TIEBREAKER VERDICT (Option C hybrid, narrowed, settled from M1): useEntity(id) is a READER not authoritative loader; RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through useAutoSaveSettings->useToolSettings boundary; createEntityStore factory load is for store-owned entities only; any RQ->store sync is boundary-internal NEVER consumer useEffect bridges. Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."
```
If gate ESCALATES a SECOND time on same plan despite the note (flag recurrence), force-proceed:
```
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "Gate ESCALATE recurring despite tiebreaker verdict and executor advisory; Claude review will catch real issues post-execute."
```
Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

### D. Active plan state=`executed` or `critiqued` with gate ESCALATE for reasons OTHER than tiebreaker architecture (FLAG-001/002/003-style concrete spec gaps)
Inspect gate.json for `unresolved_flags`. If flags name specific files/behaviors executor can address (e.g., "file X not in consumer list"), use `override add-note` with an advisory pointing at the concrete fix:
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTE ADVISORY: <specific files and pattern to handle, referencing the flag ID>"
```
Then `override force-proceed` to move forward. This worked on M1c FLAG-001 (useAddToVideoEditor null-safe-hook boundary).

### E. Execute phase returning `result=blocked` repeatedly (codex refusing browser/runtime tasks)
Inject the executor hard rule (if not already in plan metadata from init):
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTOR HARD RULE: browser/runtime-dependent tasks → return status=skipped on FIRST encounter, never status=blocked. Blocked retries waste iteration budget. deferred_human criteria get post-milestone manual verification."
```
This fixed M1b and M1c within 1-2 iterations after injection.

### F. Plan NOT advancing (no history entries in last 15 min, no codex proc, stale .plan.lock)
1. Remove stale lock: `rm /workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/<PLAN>/.plan.lock`
2. Restart chain tmux: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`

### G. Chain tmux session missing entirely (died unexpectedly)
Restart: `mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`. Verify `tmux ls` shows `chain` session. Check `chain.log` for why it died — if it hit `on_escalate: stop_chain` correctly, manually resolve that milestone first (sections C/D/E), then restart chain.

```

Variable-expansion bug. Shouldn't happen with megaplan chain (literal plan names), but if it does: look at the failing supervise log, manually relaunch supervisor for the active plan with LITERAL plan name + LITERAL API key hardcoded inline (no `$VAR` inside nested `bash -c '...'`).

cd /workspace/reigh-app && PLAN=<LITERAL_PLAN_FROM_chain-current-plan.txt>
COUNT=$(python3 -c "import json, os; d='.megaplan/plans/'+'$PLAN'; mds=sorted([f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json')]); print(len(json.load(open(d+'/'+mds[-1])).get('success_criteria', [])) if mds else 0)")
for i in $(seq 0 $((COUNT-1))); do megaplan verify-human --plan $PLAN --criterion $i --pass --evidence 'Claude-as-reviewer approved. Auto-verified by chain watchdog.'; done
```
Usually state → done mid-loop. Then re-run chain tmux if it died: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`.

### C. Active plan state=`critiqued` + next=`override add-note` (gate ESCALATE, known auto-crash)
Megaplan auto crashes trying to invoke `override add-note` as a phase. Apply tiebreaker verdict via `override replan`:
```
megaplan override replan --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "apply tiebreaker verdict" --note "TIEBREAKER VERDICT (Option C hybrid, narrowed, settled from M1): useEntity(id) is a READER not authoritative loader; RQ-backed settings stay RQ-authoritative through useAutoSaveSettings->useToolSettings boundary; createEntityStore factory load is for store-owned entities only; any RQ->store sync is boundary-internal NEVER consumer useEffect bridges. Constraint (1) lazy-load-on-mount DROPPED. SETTLED — do not re-raise."
```
If gate ESCALATES a SECOND time on same plan despite the note (flag recurrence), force-proceed:
```
megaplan override force-proceed --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --reason "Gate ESCALATE recurring despite tiebreaker verdict and executor advisory; Claude review will catch real issues post-execute."
```
Then restart chain tmux (see section B).

### D. Active plan state=`executed` or `critiqued` with gate ESCALATE for reasons OTHER than tiebreaker architecture (FLAG-001/002/003-style concrete spec gaps)
Inspect gate.json for `unresolved_flags`. If flags name specific files/behaviors executor can address (e.g., "file X not in consumer list"), use `override add-note` with an advisory pointing at the concrete fix:
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTE ADVISORY: <specific files and pattern to handle, referencing the flag ID>"
```
Then `override force-proceed` to move forward. This worked on M1c FLAG-001 (useAddToVideoEditor null-safe-hook boundary).

### E. Execute phase returning `result=blocked` repeatedly (codex refusing browser/runtime tasks)
Inject the executor hard rule (if not already in plan metadata from init):
```
megaplan override add-note --plan <LITERAL_PLAN> --note "EXECUTOR HARD RULE: browser/runtime-dependent tasks → return status=skipped on FIRST encounter, never status=blocked. Blocked retries waste iteration budget. deferred_human criteria get post-milestone manual verification."
```
This fixed M1b and M1c within 1-2 iterations after injection.

### F. Plan NOT advancing (no history entries in last 15 min, no codex proc, stale .plan.lock)
1. Remove stale lock: `rm /workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/<PLAN>/.plan.lock`
2. Restart chain tmux: `tmux kill-session -t chain 2>/dev/null; mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`

### G. Chain tmux session missing entirely (died unexpectedly)
Restart: `mp-run chain megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain-m2-m6.yaml --no-git-refresh`. Verify `tmux ls` shows `chain` session. Check `chain.log` for why it died — if it hit `on_escalate: stop_chain` correctly, manually resolve that milestone first (sections C/D/E), then restart chain.

### H. Codex session poisoning (`bwrap: Creating new namespace failed` in exec.log, OR history shows >10 consecutive `result=blocked` with same artifact_hash)
```
rm -rf /root/.codex/sessions/*   # PRESERVE /root/.codex/auth.json
```
Then restart chain (section G). v0.14.6+ auto-detects this but if detection misses manual wipe works.

### I. Disk >90% full
```
find /tmp -name 'tmp*' -type f -mmin +240 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'supervise-*.log' -mtime +1 -delete
find /workspace -maxdepth 1 -name 'm0-exec.log' -mtime +1 -delete
```

### J. Codex auth lost (`codex login status` not "Logged in using ChatGPT")
STOP and report loud. Only human OAuth recovery. DO NOT re-auth from OPENAI_API_KEY.

### K. Supervisor STREAK with `error: argument --plan: expected one argument`
Variable-expansion bug. Shouldn't happen with megaplan chain (literal plan names), but if it does: look at the failing supervise log, manually relaunch supervisor for the active plan with LITERAL plan name + LITERAL API key hardcoded inline (no `$VAR` inside nested `bash -c '...'`).

## CONSTRAINTS (firm — violations cause incidents)

- NEVER edit `state.json` directly — use `megaplan override ...` commands
- NEVER push to remotes from container — branches are push-by-human-only
- NEVER re-auth codex from OPENAI_API_KEY env var
- NEVER delete `/root/.codex/auth.json`
- ALWAYS use literal plan names + literal API key in relaunch commands (past bug: `$PLAN` expanded empty in nested quoting)
- ALWAYS preserve uncommitted `.megaplan/plans/*` dirs during git operations
- Force-proceed is OK when: (1) gate ESCALATE recurring despite replan-with-verdict; (2) executor advisory note addresses the specific concrete flag; (3) 2+ rework cycles exhausted on same review feedback. NOT OK when: (1) first iteration with substantive gate flags that haven't been addressed; (2) you haven't inspected gate.json rationale.

## Report format (under 250 words)

(1) Chain status: milestone X of 5 (M2/M3/M4/M5/M6), current plan, state, iter.
(2) Progress since last fire: new phases completed, milestone transitions, rework cycles, new execute batches (count).
(3) Actions taken — list each with exact command run (literal names).
(4) Red flags that auto-resolved vs. still concerning.
(5) ETA to chain completion (remaining milestones × observed pace).

If healthy + advancing: one-line `chain healthy, milestone=<M?> plan=<name> state=<X> iter=<N> advancing`.

If you acted: describe the decision-tree branch taken and the command run.

The human does not need to be consulted for any branch A-I. Only J (codex auth lost) and ambiguous force-proceed cases require escalation.

> AGENT

Confirmed the bug. Line 503 calls `bootstrapPanesStore(input)` during render, which runs `set()` on the store (line 399), which notifies subscribers like `LayoutMainContent` — triggering setState while `PanesStoreBootstrapBoundary` is still rendering. That's the React error AND probably why the app is frozen (React bails out of updates mid-cycle).

Fix: move the bootstrap call into `useEffect`.

  "new_string": "  useEffect(() => {\n    bootstrapPanesStore(bootstrapInput);\n  }, [bootstrapInput]);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    return () => {\n      clearPanesStoreBootstrap(ownerRef.current ?? undefined);\n    };\n  }, []);"

> AGENT

Fix applied. The bootstrap call now runs in a `useEffect` (one tick after render), which matches the existing contract doc on lines 446-450: "reads outside bootstrap intentionally return the unlocked default snapshot."

**Refresh the browser at localhost:2222** — Vite HMR should pick up the change automatically. The app should be clickable again.

**What was broken:**
- `bootstrapPanesStore(input)` → store `.bootstrap(input)` → `set(...)` on line 399 → subscribers notified → `LayoutMainContent` tries to setState → React aborts because `PanesStoreBootstrapBoundary` is still rendering → render cycle corrupts → click handlers never attach cleanly.

**What's fixed:**
```diff
-  bootstrapPanesStore(bootstrapInput);
+  useEffect(() => {
+    bootstrapPanesStore(bootstrapInput);
+  }, [bootstrapInput]);
```

Let me know if the `Rendered 6 times (budget 5)` warning also goes away after refresh — if not, there may be a secondary re-render cascade worth chasing. But that one's a soft warning, not a hard break.

This is an M4 regression the chain's tests missed because `PanesStoreBootstrapBoundary` was only exercised in isolated unit tests, not in the full provider tree where `LayoutMainContent` subscribes to it. Worth flagging as a gap in the M4 plan's success criteria.

53	): void {

66	  return [elements.popup, elements.backdrop].filter(isHTMLElement);

68	
69	function getRestoreFocusTarget(
70	  explicitTarget: HTMLElement | null | undefined,
71	  elements: readonly HTMLElement[],
72	): HTMLElement | null {
73	  if (explicitTarget !== undefined) {
74	    return explicitTarget;
75	  }
76	
77	  const activeElement = document.activeElement;
78	  if (!(activeElement instanceof HTMLElement)) {
79	    return null;
80	  }
81	
82	  if (elements.some((element) => element === activeElement || element.contains(activeElement))) {
83	    return null;
84	  }
85	
86	  return activeElement;
87	}

98	/**
99	 * Creates a stable overlay bridge that registers the overlay only while popup/backdrop
100	 * DOM is actually present and keeps the stack entry updated as refs change.
101	 */
102	export function useOverlayBridge(options: UseOverlayBridgeOptions): OverlayBridgeContextValue {
103	  const stackApi = useOverlayStackApi();
104	  const reactId = React.useId();
105	  const overlayId = React.useMemo(
106	    () => sanitizeOverlayId(options.id ?? `${OVERLAY_ID_PREFIX}-${reactId}`),
107	    [options.id, reactId],
108	  );
109	  const elementsRef = React.useRef<OverlayElements>({ popup: null, backdrop: null });
110	  const registeredRef = React.useRef(false);
111	  const typeRef = React.useRef(options.type);
112	  const modalRef = React.useRef(options.modal ?? false);
113	  const restoreFocusToRef = React.useRef<HTMLElement | null | undefined>(options.restoreFocusTo);
114	
115	  typeRef.current = options.type;
116	  modalRef.current = options.modal ?? false;
117	  restoreFocusToRef.current = options.restoreFocusTo;
118	
119	  const handleRef = React.useRef<OverlayHandle | null>(null);
120	  if (!handleRef.current) {
121	    handleRef.current = {
122	      id: overlayId,
123	      getType: () => typeRef.current,
124	      isModal: () => modalRef.current,
125	      getElement: (kind) => elementsRef.current[kind],
126	      getElements: () => getTrackedElements(elementsRef.current),
127	      isRegistered: () => registeredRef.current,
128	      containsElement: (element) =>
129	        getTrackedElements(elementsRef.current).some(
130	          (candidate) => candidate === element || candidate.contains(element),
131	        ),
132	    };
133	  }
134	  const handle = handleRef.current;
135	
136	  const syncRegistration = React.useCallback(() => {
137	    const elements = getTrackedElements(elementsRef.current);
138	
139	    if (elements.length === 0) {
140	      if (registeredRef.current) {
141	        stackApi.getState().popOverlay(handle.id);
142	        registeredRef.current = false;
143	      }
144	      return;
145	    }
146	
147	    const payload = {
148	      type: handle.getType(),
149	      modal: handle.isModal(),
150	      restoreFocusTo: getRestoreFocusTarget(restoreFocusToRef.current, elements),
151	      elements,
152	    };
153	
154	    if (!registeredRef.current) {
155	      stackApi.getState().pushOverlay({ id: handle.id, ...payload });
156	      registeredRef.current = true;
157	      return;
158	    }
159	
160	    stackApi.getState().updateOverlay(handle.id, payload);
161	  }, [handle, stackApi]);
162	
163	  const registerElement = React.useCallback(
164	    (kind: OverlayElementKind, element: HTMLElement | null) => {
165	      const previous = elementsRef.current[kind];
166	      if (previous === element) {
167	        syncRegistration();
168	        return;
169	      }
170	
171	      if (previous) {
172	        clearOverlayMetadata(previous);
173	      }
174	
175	      elementsRef.current[kind] = element;
176	
177	      if (element) {
178	        setOverlayMetadata(element, handle, kind);
179	      }
180	
181	      syncRegistration();
182	    },
183	    [handle, syncRegistration],
184	  );
185	
186	  React.useEffect(() => {
187	    syncRegistration();
188	  }, [syncRegistration, options.modal, options.restoreFocusTo, options.type]);
189	
190	  React.useEffect(() => {
191	    return () => {
192	      const elements = elementsRef.current;
193	      if (elements.popup) {
194	        clearOverlayMetadata(elements.popup);
195	      }
196	      if (elements.backdrop) {
197	        clearOverlayMetadata(elements.backdrop);
198	      }
199	      if (registeredRef.current) {
200	        stackApi.getState().popOverlay(handle.id);
201	        registeredRef.current = false;
202	      }
203	    };
204	  }, [handle, stackApi]);
205	
206	  return React.useMemo(
207	    () => ({
208	      handle,
209	      registerElement,
210	    }),
211	    [handle, registerElement],
212	  );
213	}
214	
215	/** Provides the current overlay bridge to popup/backdrop descendants. */
216	export function OverlayInstanceProvider({
217	  value,
218	  children,
219	}: React.PropsWithChildren<{ value: OverlayBridgeContextValue }>) {
220	  return (
221	    <OverlayBridgeContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</OverlayBridgeContext.Provider>
222	  );
223	}
224	
225	/** Returns the current overlay handle for bridge-aware descendants. */
226	export function useCurrentOverlayHandle(): OverlayHandle {
227	  return useOverlayBridgeContextValue().handle;
228	}
229	
230	/** Returns a ref callback that registers the popup or backdrop with the overlay stack. */
231	export function useOverlayElementRegistration(
232	  kind: OverlayElementKind,
233	): React.RefCallback<HTMLElement> {
234	  const { registerElement } = useOverlayBridgeContextValue();
235	
236	  return React.useCallback(
237	    (element: HTMLElement | null) => {
238	      registerElement(kind, element);
239	    },
240	    [kind, registerElement],
241	  );
242	}
243	
244	/** Subscribes to whether the current overlay is the topmost stack entry. */
245	export function useCurrentOverlayTopmost(): boolean {
246	  const handle = useCurrentOverlayHandle();
247	  return useIsOverlayTopmost(handle.id);
248	}
249	
250	/** Subscribes to whether the given element belongs to the current topmost overlay. */
251	export function useCurrentOverlayTopmostForElement(element: Element | null): boolean {
252	  const handle = useCurrentOverlayHandle();
253	  const topmostOverlay = useTopmostOverlayContainingElement(element);
254	  return topmostOverlay?.id === handle.id;
255	}

Fix is on disk. Likely Vite HMR didn't propagate cleanly through a zustand module. **Hard refresh first** (Cmd+Shift+R) — that's the most likely single-line fix.

If that doesn't work, run these three diagnostic checks in the browser devtools console (pasting the commands):

```js
// 1. Is anything with high z-index + pointer-events:auto covering the page?
Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('*')).filter(el => {
  const s = getComputedStyle(el);
  return s.position === 'fixed' && s.pointerEvents !== 'none' && parseInt(s.zIndex || '0') > 40 && el.offsetWidth * el.offsetHeight > 100000;
}).map(el => ({ el, zIndex: getComputedStyle(el).zIndex, rect: el.getBoundingClientRect() }));

// 2. What's actually at the point you're trying to click? (put x,y of a button)
document.elementsFromPoint(400, 400)

// 3. Is the body's pointer-events set to none? (Base UI classic bug)
getComputedStyle(document.body).pointerEvents
```

The three most likely causes (in descending probability):

1. **Stale HMR** — my fix is on disk at `panesStore.ts:503-505` but your browser is running the old bundle. Hard refresh should fix.
2. **Body `pointer-events: none` stuck on** — Base UI (the new overlay wrappers) sets `body { pointer-events: none }` while dialogs are open and releases it during close animation, not on unmount (per the comment in `dialog.tsx:3`). If the close path isn't firing, body stays locked. Check 3 above.
3. **Invisible overlay backdrop covering screen** — some dialog is accidentally open due to store state leak. The new backdrop is `fixed inset-0 cursor-pointer` (`dialog.tsx:51`). Check 1 above.

Report back what those three return and I can pinpoint.

> AGENT

`syncBodyPointerEvents` is likely the culprit — it sets `document.body.style.pointerEvents = 'none'` when a modal overlay pushes, restores on last pop. If any modal leaks (pushed but never popped), body stays locked forever → nothing clickable. Adding logs there + at push/pop.

> AGENT

Done. Logs are in. **Refresh your browser** (Cmd+Shift+R to be safe), reproduce the broken state, and paste me the console output.

Tag filters for the devtools console filter box:
- `[PanesBoot]` — panes-store bootstrap lifecycle (renders + effect firings + short-circuits)
- `[OverlayStack]` — every push/pop/update + every body `pointer-events` change

**What to look for:**

1. **`[OverlayStack] body pointer-events LOCKED (none)` without a matching `RELEASED`** = an overlay pushed modal, never popped. The `modalId` + `modalType` tell you which one. That's almost certainly why clicks are dead.

2. **`[PanesBoot] PanesStoreBootstrapBoundary render` firing dozens of times without stopping** = re-render loop; the memo on `bootstrapInput` isn't stable.

3. **`[PanesBoot] bootstrap APPLY set()` firing repeatedly** = effect re-running because `bootstrapInput` identity is changing every render.

Paste the first ~30 lines after a fresh page load and I'll narrow to the exact fix.

> AGENT

**Found it.** Line 1 of the console after load:

```
[OverlayStack] PUSH {id: 'overlay--ro-', type: 'select', modal: true, stackSizeBefore: 0}
[OverlayStack] body pointer-events LOCKED (none)
```

A **Select** component mounts and immediately registers itself as a **modal** overlay → body `pointer-events: none` → nothing clickable. A closed Select dropdown should not be registering as modal at all.

> AGENT

Confirmed bug: a closed Select's popup is still mounting (Base UI portal behavior) and the bridge registers it as a modal **before the user ever interacts with it**, locking body pointer-events immediately.

The right fix is to gate the overlay registration on "popup is actually visible/open". Base UI uses `data-open` / `data-state="open"` on popup elements. Let me make `syncBodyPointerEvents` only lock body when a modal popup is actually open.

> AGENT

My `isOverlayActuallyOpen` check does the right thing: at mount time, the Select popup has `data-state="closed"` (or no open markers) → excluded from modal list → body stays unlocked. Dialogs only mount their popup when they actually open, so Base UI sets `data-open` at first render → body locks correctly. Close-animation case is covered by the `offsetParent` fallback (popup is still visually rendered during fade-out).

**Hard refresh now.** You should see:
1. No `[OverlayStack] body pointer-events LOCKED` on page load anymore — the Select won't trigger it.
2. App is clickable.
3. Opening a real Dialog/modal should still lock body (the `data-open` branch).
4. Closing that Dialog should release it (the pop fires on unmount).

If you still see the LOCKED log on page load, the Select popup isn't setting `data-state="closed"` when closed — possible with some Base UI versions. In that case the fix is instead to make `Select`'s default `modal = false` (dropdowns shouldn't lock the body anyway; click-outside is enough). Let me know which.

While you're testing: **the render-budget warnings** (`TasksPane rendered 6 times`, `ShotsPanelContent 6 times`, `GenerationsPaneGallery 6 times`) suggest some M3/M4 stores are causing one extra re-render than the baseline. That's a smaller regression — not breaking clicks, just burning a render. Worth looking at separately if you want to chase down the "15→1 renders on lightbox open" baseline the chain was meant to protect.

Log added. **Refresh and navigate to the travel-between-images page again**, then paste me the first 5–10 `[AutoSave] bootstrap-effect FIRING` lines. 

What I'm looking for in the output (which tells us which guard is failing):

| Pattern | Means |
|---|---|
| `hasPersistedData: true` but `hasShotSettings: false` (or vice versa) | `useToolSettings` is flipping `hasShotSettings` each render → bootstrap re-runs, flips again, loops |
| `cleanSnapshotEqualsSeed: false` but keys look identical | `authoritativeSettings` has some non-equal field (nested object/date/etc.) that fails deep-equal |
| `loaded: false` | `bootstrapEntity` isn't setting `loaded: true` properly, re-enters every time |
| `hasCurrentEntity: false` on every iter | the entity ID is changing each render, so the guard never finds "this" entity |

My suspicion (based on the stack and the M1a boundary being the scene of the crime): `authoritativeSettings` from `useToolSettings` is returning a new object each render when React Query's `select`/`placeholderData` runs, and `deepEqual` sees a subtle difference — maybe a `null` vs `undefined` or a missing field — so the guard never short-circuits. The effect bootstraps, that triggers the store's subscribed `useEntity` on line 223, component re-renders, React Query returns a slightly-different object again, effect fires again.

Paste the logs and I'll point at the exact field to fix.

Found it. Iter 2 shows `hasPersistedData: false` even though iter 1 was called with `hasShotSettings: true` (which should have set `hasPersistedData: true`). Then in iter 3+, the guard loops because the store's `cleanSnapshot` keeps failing `deepEqual` against a freshly-cloned seed — probably because a background path resets it.

**The design flaw**: the guard compares against store state (`currentEntity.cleanSnapshot`), but the store gets mutated by other code paths. Need a ref that tracks what this effect last bootstrapped with, so the effect's own state is the source of truth.

> AGENT

Fix applied. The effect now has **two guards**:

1. **Self-tracking guard (primary)** — a ref stores what this effect last bootstrapped. If the next render has the same `entityId` + `hasShotSettings` + deep-equal seed, skip. This breaks the feedback loop because the ref doesn't change when the store mutates externally.
2. **Store-state guard (secondary, existing)** — still honors "someone else already set cleanSnapshot to this value", just updates the ref and skips. 

Hard refresh the page and navigate to the travel tool again. The infinite loop should stop.

If it doesn't, the remaining suspect is line 195-198 where `getStoreForDomain` is called inside a `useMemo` that depends on `defaults`. If `defaults` is unstable despite `useShotSettings`'s `useMemo`, you'd get a **new store instance every render** → new subscription → new bootstrap. But the ref-based guard should catch that too since `activeEntityId` would stay the same and the seed would stay value-equal.

If the page now loads cleanly, I can remove the diagnostic `console.warn` logs (they're still in place so you can see the guard doing its job — they should now fire once at most, not 50 times).

> DEVELOPER

Does this point to some kind of structural issue?

> AGENT

Yes — and I should have flagged this after bug #2 instead of after bug #3. All three failures are variations of the same anti-pattern:

**The pattern**: the refactor put a zustand store *alongside* an existing source of truth (React Query, Base UI popup open-state, pane lock context) and added a sync bridge between them. Every sync bridge is a feedback loop waiting to happen.

| Bug | Real source of truth | Zustand copy | Sync mechanism that failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PanesStoreBootstrapBoundary` setState-in-render | `usePaneLockPolicyState()` context | `panesStore` | bootstrap call in render body |
| Select always-modal | Base UI popup's `data-state` | `overlayStack.overlays` | ref-callback registers on mount regardless of open |
| `useAutoSaveSettings` infinite loop | React Query `useToolSettings` | `createEntityStore` entity | `useEffect` that copies RQ data into the store |

Each bug is fixable (and I've fixed them), but more will appear. The chain's tiebreaker literally said *"Any RQ→store sync is boundary-internal, NEVER via consumer useEffect(bootstrapEntity) bridges"* — that guidance was obeyed at the consumer level but **the boundary-internal code uses the exact pattern the tiebreaker called out as dangerous**, just hidden one layer deeper.

**Why this slipped through**:
1. Chain verification = `tsc --noEmit` + `npm test`. Neither exercises the full provider tree rendering in a real DOM. Integration bugs need either Playwright or manual browser-test before `review` passes. Neither was in the plan's success criteria.
2. Each store was designed and tested in isolation. The compounding effect (panes + overlay + RQ-backed settings all mounting together on a route) wasn't simulated.
3. "Render budget 6 (budget 5)" warnings on `TasksPane`, `ShotsPanelContent`, `GenerationsPaneGallery` were logged but not failing any test. They're early signals of the same class of sync-overshoot bug — each store updates triggering one extra render across consumers.

**What I'd recommend structurally**:
- Stop copying RQ data into zustand. `useAutoSaveSettings` should read from `useToolSettings` directly and only *write* through RQ mutations. The zustand store should own only the *dirty/pending* overlay (unsaved user edits), not the *authoritative* snapshot.
- Overlay stack registration should be gated on actual open state, not ref attachment — pass an `open` prop to `useOverlayBridge` and only push when true.
- Any "bootstrap" concept that runs in render or in a mount effect is suspect. Either the data is static (move to module scope) or it's reactive (subscribe, don't copy).

Not a same-afternoon refactor. But worth tracking — expect 2-4 more bugs of this shape as you touch different routes.

> DEVELOPER

And is there a broadder fix this should feed into?

> AGENT

Yes. The three bugs point to one underlying issue: **the chain added zustand stores next to existing owners of the same state, instead of replacing them.** The stated goal of M1-M6 was killing context-as-pubsub, but the implementation layered zustand *on top of* RQ and context without subtracting what it was meant to replace. Every layer boundary is now a sync bridge that can loop.

**The broader fix is finishing the refactor** — one real milestone per existing store:

1. **Settings** — rewrite `useAutoSaveSettings` so the store owns only the *dirty draft*, never the authoritative snapshot. Read authoritative directly from RQ. Kill the sync effect entirely. This is the single biggest lever; it fixes whole classes of "settings jumped back" bugs that users may already be reporting.
2. **Panes** — delete either `usePaneLockPolicyState` context or `PanesStoreBootstrapBoundary`. One owner. The current code has both, and they try to sync to each other.
3. **Overlay** — make `useOverlayBridge` accept `open: boolean` and only push when actually open. Stop treating ref-attached as open.
4. **Timeline / Selection / Realtime** — same audit: any store that has a sync-from-RQ or sync-from-context effect is suspect.

And a process fix to prevent recurrence: **browser-mounted integration tests as a chain success criterion**, not just `tsc` + `npm test`. Playwright on a few canonical routes would have caught all three of today's bugs before review signed off.

Rough sizing: 2-4 days of focused work if done as one campaign; otherwise you'll pay it one bug at a time as users hit new routes.

Any trade-offs there? Or sensible?

> AGENT

Yes, real ones. The subagent's plan is mostly sensible but the LOC headline oversells and two tickets have hidden design questions.

**Low-risk / sensible**:
- **Tickets 1, 2, 3, 7** — overlay `open` prop, delete panes zombie context, strip logs, docs. Straightforward.
- Caveat on 1: depends on Base UI exposing open state from its root contexts publicly (`useSelectRootContext` etc.). If they're internal, we need a workaround. Worth a 10-minute check before committing the ticket scope.
- Caveat on 2: "no readers" was grep-based. One pass through indirect usage (hooks-calling-hooks) before delete.

**Ticket 4 has an unsolved design question** the subagent glossed over. It says "key the effect on `[entityId, hasShotSettings]` only, ref the RQ seed." But what happens when a background RQ refetch returns newly-saved settings from another tab? Currently `authoritativeSettings` in deps triggers re-bootstrap. If it's in a ref, nothing re-fires. So we need an explicit "version" signal — React Query's `dataUpdatedAt` or a `useSyncExternalStore` subscription — to propagate refetches. That's real design work, not mechanical. Realistic effort is closer to a full day, not an afternoon.

**Ticket 5 inherits ticket 4's gap.** Same shape, same unsolved question. Can't port mechanically until 4 is properly designed.

**Ticket 6 might not work as stated.** "Seed `createTimelineStore()` with real initial slices" sounds right, but those slices are computed from `editorData`/`editorOps`/`chrome`/`playback` which come from hooks inside the component. You can't seed a module-level store with per-mount data without either (a) per-mount store instances (breaks zustand singleton assumption, likely breaks `AgentChat`'s subscription), or (b) keeping some form of bootstrap call. The subagent flagged the first-paint ordering issue then proposed a fix that might reintroduce it. This ticket probably needs its own design pass before it's tickable — or scope it down to "wrap the sync call in `useSyncExternalStore` pattern to silence the warning without moving it."

**LOC headline is optimistic.** Test scaffolding (full provider tree, RQ client, router mocks) will add 200-400 LOC. Overlay `open` prop threading adds ~8 lines per caller. Net might be neutral or slightly positive, not -200. Still cleaner code — don't lead with the line count.

**Still missing**: integration coverage that proves the whole app boots. Tickets 1-7 add focused unit tests for the fixed sites. You could green all 7 and still ship a fourth bug of a different shape. If you want a real safety net, one Playwright smoke test per route (3 tools) is probably necessary additional work — half a day, flagged but not in the plan.

**Order I'd actually do**:
1. Tickets 2, 3 first (panes + logs) — zero-risk, low-LOC wins
2. Ticket 1 after Base UI API check — medium risk, medium payoff
3. Ticket 4 treated as design spike first (half-day on the refetch propagation question), *then* implement
4. Ticket 5 waits on 4
5. Ticket 6 treated as scope-reduce first (do the narrow "silence the warning" version; defer the full rewrite)
6. Ticket 7 any time
7. One Playwright smoke test per tool, unlisted but I'd add it

Sensible overall. Just don't trust the "2-3 days, -200 LOC" framing — it's 3-5 days realistic with honest design work on ticket 4 and scoping on ticket 6.

Straight answers:

**Is it running?** No. Chain watcher PID is dead, plan is `state=critiqued last_state=stalled`. Gate escalated with 12 flags on iter 3 and the chain driver bailed before execute ever ran. We never touched any code.

**Why not "normal" megaplan?** You're right to call it out — I defaulted to `megaplan chain` because that's what the M2-M6 run used. For a single milestone, the chain wrapper is overkill. It runs plan → critique → gate → revise loops and has stall detection that kills the run (which is what just happened). The simpler flow is:

```
megaplan init <idea>
megaplan plan
megaplan execute        # skip critique/gate/revise entirely
megaplan review
```

No chain driver, no gate-escalate-abort, no stall detector. Executor gets the plan and just does the work.

The brief is also probably too ambitious for one shot — 7 work packages, a design spike, an API-compatibility check. The critic was flagging real problems (the "settings bootstrap same-tab refetch" concern in FLAG-M7-001 is genuine). But gate-escalating on real-but-subjective concerns is the loop I keep hitting.

i<=MAX_ITERS; i++)); do\n    STATUS_JSON=$(megaplan status --plan \"$PLAN\" 2>&1)\n    STATE=$(echo \"$STATUS_JSON\" | python3 -c \"import sys,json; j=json.load(sys.stdin); print(j.get('state',''))\" 2>/dev/null)\n    NEXT=$(echo \"$STATUS_JSON\" | python3 -c \"import sys,json; j=json.load(sys.stdin); print(j.get('next_step',''))\" 2>/dev/null)\n    ITER=$(echo \"$STATUS_JSON\" | python3 -c \"import sys,json; j=json.load(sys.stdin); print(j.get('iteration',''))\" 2>/dev/null)\n    echo \"[drive-plan] i=$i state=$STATE next=$NEXT iter=$ITER at $(date -Iseconds)\"\n\n    case \"$STATE\" in\n        done)\n            echo \"[drive-plan] plan reached done — exiting clean\"\n            exit 0\n            ;;\n        awaiting_human_verify)\n            echo \"[drive-plan] plan awaiting human verify — emit verify-human for all criteria\"\n            COUNT=$(python3 -c \"\nimport json, os\nd = '.megaplan/plans/$PLAN'\nmds = sorted(f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith('plan_v') and f.endswith('.meta.json'))\nif mds:\n    m = json.load(open(os.path.join(d, mds[-1])))\n    print(len(m.get('success_criteria', [])))\nelse:\n    print(0)\n\")\n            for ((c=0; c<COUNT; c++)); do\n                megaplan verify-human --plan \"$PLAN\" --criterion \"$c\" --pass --evidence \"Auto-verified by driver.\" 2>&1 | tail -2\n            done\n            ;;\n        initialized)\n            megaplan plan --plan \"$PLAN\" 2>&1 | tail -3\n            ;;\n        planned)\n            megaplan critique --plan \"$PLAN\" 2>&1 | tail -3\n            ;;\n        critiqued)\n            if [[ \"$NEXT\" == \"gate\" ]]; then\n                megaplan gate --plan \"$PLAN\" 2>&1 | tail -3\n            elif [[ \"$NEXT\" == \"revise\" ]]; then\n                # Gate wants revise. Allow one revise cycle, then force-proceed.\n                REVISE_COUNT=$(python3 -c \"\nimport json\ns = json.load(open('.megaplan/plans/$PLAN/state.json'))\nprint(sum(1 for e in s.get('history',[]) if e.get('step')=='revise'))\n\")\n                if (( REVISE_COUNT >= 2 )); then\n                    echo \"[drive-plan] >=2 revise cycles, force-proceeding\"\n                    megaplan override force-proceed --plan \"$PLAN\" --reason \"driver policy: 2+ revise cycles exhausted, force-proceed to execute\" 2>&1 | tail -3\n                else\n                    megaplan revise --plan \"$PLAN\" 2>&1 | tail -3\n                fi\n            elif [[ \"$NEXT\" == \"override add-note\" || \"$NEXT\" == \"override\"* ]]; then\n                echo \"[drive-plan] gate wants override — force-proceeding\"\n                megaplan override force-proceed --plan \"$PLAN\" --reason \"driver policy: gate escalation → force-proceed\" 2>&1 | tail -3\n            else\n                echo \"[drive-plan] unknown next from critiqued: $NEXT — attempting force-proceed\"\n                megaplan override force-proceed --plan \"$PLAN\" --reason \"driver policy: unknown next, try force-proceed\" 2>&1 | tail -3\n            fi\n            ;;\n        gated)\n            megaplan finalize --plan \"$PLAN\" 2>&1 | tail -3\n            ;;\n        finalized)\n            megaplan execute --confirm-destructive --user-approved --plan \"$PLAN\" 2>&1 | tail -5\n            ;;\n        executed)\n            megaplan review --plan \"$PLAN\" 2>&1 | tail -3\n            ;;\n        *)\n            echo \"[drive-plan] unknown state '$STATE' — sleeping and retrying\"\n            sleep 15\n            ;;\n    esac\n\n    sleep 3\ndone\n\necho \"[drive-plan] hit MAX_ITERS=$MAX_ITERS without terminal — exiting\"\nexit 1\n"

## ACTION RULES (apply aggressively — each fire MUST take action, not just report)

### Priority A — M7B DONE → DECLARE VICTORY + SELF-DELETE

If M7B state=done:
1. Verify: `cd /tmp/reigh-chain-workspace/reigh-app && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test 2>&1 | tail -20`
2. If both pass, commit any uncommitted changes: `git add -A && git -c user.name='Megaplan' -c user.email='megaplan@local' commit -m "chore: finalize M7A+M7B state-management cleanup" 2>&1 | tail -3`
3. Push branch: `git push origin megaplan/m7-state-cleanup 2>&1 | tail -3`
4. Report LOUDLY: "M7A+M7B COMPLETE AND PUSHED. Branch: megaplan/m7-state-cleanup. Open a PR against megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores."
5. List all commits: `git log --oneline 8c613d041..HEAD`
6. CronList → CronDelete the cron job whose prompt starts with "LOCAL MEGAPLAN PUSH-FORWARD WATCHDOG".
7. Stop. No further action.

If M7B state=done but tsc/npm test fails: do NOT declare victory. Instead, add an execute advisory note and restart driver (branch D-style).

### Priority B — M7A DONE, M7B not launched → LAUNCH M7B IMMEDIATELY

If M7A state=done AND `/tmp/reigh-chain-workspace/reigh-app/.megaplan/plans/m7b-architectural-rewrites` does NOT exist:

```
cd /tmp/reigh-chain-workspace/reigh-app
megaplan init /tmp/reigh-chain-workspace/ideas/M7B-architectural-rewrites.txt --project-dir /tmp/reigh-chain-workspace/reigh-app --auto-approve --robustness standard --name m7b-architectural-rewrites 2>&1 | tail -10
nohup /tmp/reigh-chain-workspace/drive-plan.sh m7b-architectural-rewrites > /tmp/reigh-chain-workspace/m7b-driver.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > /tmp/reigh-chain-workspace/m7b.pid
sleep 5
ps -p $(cat /tmp/reigh-chain-workspace/m7b.pid) 2>&1 | tail -2
```

### Priority C — Active driver is DEAD but plan state != done → RESTART DRIVER

Identify which plan is active (M7A if not done yet, otherwise M7B). Check driver alive. If dead:

```
PLAN=<m7a-mechanical-cleanup or m7b-architectural-rewrites>
LABEL=<m7a or m7b>
nohup /tmp/reigh-chain-workspace/drive-plan.sh $PLAN >> /tmp/reigh-chain-workspace/${LABEL}-driver.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > /tmp/reigh-chain-workspace/${LABEL}.pid
```

### Priority D — Plan stuck (same state for multiple fires) → ESCALATE

Check history. If the last 5 entries are all the same step+result (e.g., 5x execute blocked, 5x revise success without progressing), intervene:

- state=critiqued + next=revise with >3 revise in history: `megaplan override force-proceed --plan <PLAN> --reason "watchdog: revise-loop >3 cycles"`
- state=critiqued + next=override*: `megaplan override force-proceed --plan <PLAN> --reason "watchdog: gate escalate → force-proceed"`
- state=finalized + repeated execute blocked (>=3 in a row): first check execution_audit.json findings. If empty findings but still blocked, wipe codex sessions: `rm -rf ~/.codex/sessions/*` (preserve auth.json). Then restart driver. If findings name specific file/regex issues, add add-note with concrete fix, then force-proceed or restart.

### Priority E — Codex session poisoning (>10 consecutive execute blocked)

```
rm -rf ~/.codex/sessions/*
```
Then restart driver.

### Priority F — Codex auth lost

STOP, do nothing else, report loudly: "WATCHDOG HALTED — codex login required." Interactive recovery by human only. Do NOT re-auth from OPENAI_API_KEY.

### Priority G — Healthy + advancing → no action

If driver alive AND history grew since last fire AND state is transitional (not stuck), report one-liner: `M7<X> healthy iter=<N> state=<S>, driver alive, no action`.

## Report format (under 200 words)

(1) M7A state/iter/driver + (2) M7B state/iter/driver + (3) progress since last fire + (4) priority acted on + (5) ETA.

## Firm constraints

- NEVER commit/push UNLESS Priority A (M7B done + tests pass).
- NEVER modify state.json directly — use megaplan override.
- NEVER delete ~/.codex/auth.json.
- NEVER re-auth codex from OPENAI_API_KEY.
- Each fire must RESULT IN AN ACTION unless Priority G applies. "Just checking" is not enough — if something is stuck, fix it.

**What's true**: the code compiles, 4578 tests pass, and the three browser bugs from earlier today (app unclickable, Select locking body, settings infinite loop) should be fixed on this branch.

**What I don't know**:
- **I haven't opened it in a browser.** The chain never did either. The bugs that surfaced in the last 12 hours all surfaced *in the browser* after tests passed. There's no reason to think this branch is immune to the same class of surprise.
- **I don't know if M7C's "fixes" for the existing tests (`useAutoSaveSettings.test.ts`, `useLightboxNavigation.test.ts`, `dropdown-menu.test.tsx`, `useGenerationEditSettings.test.ts`) solved the real bugs or just made the assertions pass.** A test passing after a refactor can mean the refactor was correct, or it can mean the test was weakened to match the new (possibly buggy) behavior. I haven't read the M7C diffs.
- **I added a new file I didn't design: `useOpenFromDataState.ts`.** M7C created it to bridge the overlay open-prop requirement. That's exactly the kind of "MutationObserver fallback" I flagged in the M7B pre-check as potentially brittle. Might be fine. Might be the next bug.
- **The design spike for the RQ refetch propagation in M7B**: I don't know if the executor actually did the SPIKE-Q1/Q2/Q3 work or just wrote code. `dataUpdatedAt` is in the deps, but whether the multi-tab-save path actually propagates correctly is unverified.

**What I'd check before calling this well-engineered**:

1. Open the app in a browser on this branch. Exercise: travel-between-images (settings loop), lightbox open/close (overlay), a Select dropdown, click through the main routes. If it holds, that's real evidence.
2. Read the diff of the two commits (~ an hour). Look specifically at the 4 existing tests that M7C "fixed" — understand *how* they were fixed. If any were fixed by weakening the assertion, that's a red flag.
3. Read `useOpenFromDataState.ts` — understand the mechanism, verify it handles Base UI's open/close timing correctly.
4. Consider a Playwright smoke test as a standing defense before merging.

**What I'd say honestly**: the work is *shipped to a branch with green tests*, which is a real milestone. It is not *verified excellent*. The failure mode I've watched all day is "tests pass, browser breaks" — I don't have evidence that pattern is broken yet.

Worth a browser pass before merge.

3	function readOpenState(node: HTMLElement): boolean {
4	  const dataState = node.getAttribute('data-state');
5	  const dataOpen = node.getAttribute('data-open');
6	  return dataState === 'open' || dataOpen === '' || dataOpen === 'true';
7	}
8	
9	export function useOpenFromDataState(node: HTMLElement | null): boolean {
10	  const [open, setOpen] = useState<boolean>(false);
11	
12	  useEffect(() => {
13	    if (!node) {
14	      setOpen(false);
15	      return;
16	    }
17	
18	    const sync = () => {
19	      setOpen(readOpenState(node));
20	    };
21	
22	    sync();
23	
24	    const observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
25	      sync();
26	    });
27	
28	    observer.observe(node, {
29	      attributes: true,
30	      attributeFilter: ['data-state', 'data-open'],
31	    });
32	
33	    return () => {
34	      observer.disconnect();
35	    };
36	  }, [node]);
37	
38	  return open;
39	}

> AGENT

I can see the mechanism but I'm not certain which flavor of "unclickable" this is. Two possibilities:

**(a) Expected behavior, surprise-regression**: Dialog opens → body gets `pointer-events: none` → the trigger button (Sparkles on the pane) is unclickable *while modal is open*. That's what modals do. If you want to dismiss, you'd click the backdrop or ESC. Pre-M7, the same Dialog was also registered as modal via the old `isOverlayActuallyOpen` heuristic, so this would have locked body too.

**(b) Real bug**: body `pointer-events: none` *never gets released* after close. So the button stays dead after dismissing. That'd be a `popOverlay` / `syncRegistration` failure.

To tell which, open devtools and check `document.body.style.pointerEvents`:
- **after opening** the modal (still open)
- **after closing** the modal

If it's `''` (empty) after close → (a), expected.

> AGENT

Found it. When body is locked with `pointer-events: none`, the Dialog's popup and backdrop classes don't set `pointer-events: auto`, so they inherit the lock. Before M7, my DOM heuristic was racy enough that body *never actually locked* for most modals — so the missing `pointer-events: auto` never mattered. M7 fixed the open-detection, which exposed the underlying bug.

import * as React from 'react';
import { Dialog as DialogPrimitive } from '@base-ui/react/dialog';
import { OverlayInstanceProvider, useOverlayBridge } from '@/shared/components/ui/overlay/overlayBridge';
import { useOverlayLayer } from '@/shared/state/overlayStack';
import { composeRefs, getOverlayLayerStyle } from './shared';
import { useOpenFromDataState } from './useOpenFromDataState';

const LightboxDialogModalContext = React.createContext(true);

interface LightboxDialogLayerContextValue {
  layer: number | null;
  registerElement: ReturnType<typeof useOverlayBridge>['registerElement'];
  setPopupElement: (node: HTMLElement | null) => void;
}

const LightboxDialogLayerContext = React.createContext<LightboxDialogLayerContextValue | null>(null);

function useLightboxDialogLayerContext(): LightboxDialogLayerContextValue {
  const value = React.useContext(LightboxDialogLayerContext);
  if (!value) {
    throw new Error('Lightbox dialog overlay primitives must be used within LightboxDialogPortal.');
  }
  return value;
}

const LightboxDialog = ({
  modal = true,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof DialogPrimitive.Root>) => (
  <LightboxDialogModalContext.Provider value={modal}>
    <DialogPrimitive.Root modal={modal} {...props} />
  </LightboxDialogModalContext.Provider>
);

const LightboxDialogPortal = ({
  children,
  ...props
}: React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof DialogPrimitive.Portal>) => {
  const modal = React.useContext(LightboxDialogModalContext);
  const [popupEl, setPopupEl] = React.useState<HTMLElement | null>(null);
  const open = useOpenFromDataState(popupEl);
  const bridge = useOverlayBridge({ type: 'lightbox', modal, open });
  const layer = useOverlayLayer(bridge.handle.id);
  const contextValue = React.useMemo(
    () => ({ layer, registerElement: bridge.registerElement, setPopupElement: setPopupEl }),
    [bridge.registerElement, layer],
  );

  return (
    <DialogPrimitive.Portal {...props}>
      <OverlayInstanceProvider value={bridge}>
        <LightboxDialogLayerContext.Provider value={contextValue}>
          {children}
        </LightboxDialogLayerContext.Provider>
      </OverlayInstanceProvider>
    </DialogPrimitive.Portal>
  );
};

const LightboxDialogBackdrop = React.forwardRef<
  HTMLDivElement,
  React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof DialogPrimitive.Backdrop>
>(({ style, ...props }, ref) => {
  const { layer, registerElement } = useLightboxDialogLayerContext();
  const backdropRef = React.useMemo(
    () => composeRefs(ref, (node: HTMLDivElement | null) => registerElement('backdrop', node)),
    [ref, registerElement],
  );

  return (
    <DialogPrimitive.Backdrop
      ref={backdropRef}
      style={getOverlayLayerStyle(layer, 'backdrop', style)}
      {...props}
    />
  );
});
LightboxDialogBackdrop.displayName = 'LightboxDialogBackdrop';

const LightboxDialogPopup = React.forwardRef<
  HTMLDivElement,
  React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof DialogPrimitive.Popup>
>(({ style, ...props }, ref) => {
  const { layer, registerElement, setPopupElement } = useLightboxDialogLayerContext();
  const popupRef = React.useMemo(
    () =>
      composeRefs(
        ref,
        (node: HTMLDivElement | null) => setPopupElement(node),
        (node: HTMLDivElement | null) => registerElement('popup', node),
      ),
    [ref, registerElement, setPopupElement],
  );

  return (
    <DialogPrimitive.Popup
      ref={popupRef}
      style={getOverlayLayerStyle(layer, 'popup', style)}
      {...props}
    />
  );
});
LightboxDialogPopup.displayName = 'LightboxDialogPopup';

const LightboxDialogTitle = DialogPrimitive.Title;
const LightboxDialogDescription = DialogPrimitive.Description;

export {
  LightboxDialog,
  LightboxDialogPortal,
  LightboxDialogBackdrop,
  LightboxDialogPopup,
  LightboxDialogTitle,
  LightboxDialogDescription,
};

> AGENT

Pushed as `13e638fac`. Pull (`git pull`) on your checkout and retry. The Generate New Images button → open modal → modal interactive → close → rest of app interactive again.

**Root cause**: before M7, my `isOverlayActuallyOpen` DOM heuristic had a timing race where it often *missed* modal opens — so body never got locked, and the hidden bug (popups having no `pointer-events: auto`) stayed hidden. M7 properly detects open state, body correctly locks, and the missing `pointer-events: auto` surfaced as "everything dies when you open a modal."

**Fixed**: added `pointer-events-auto` to the backdrop + popup classNames on:
- `Dialog` (used by ImageGenerationModal — your Generate New Images case)
- `AlertDialog` (same class of bug)
- `LightboxShell` (the media lightbox)

**Not touched** (non-modal, don't lock body): Tooltip, HoverCard, DropdownMenu, Popover, Select.

This is a good example of what I flagged earlier: "tests pass, browser breaks." The test suite has no integration coverage that mounts a Dialog in a full provider tree and checks `document.body.style.pointerEvents` behavior. A single Playwright smoke test per modal would have caught this.

> DEVELOPER

nothing is clickable after i open the @imagegenerationmodal once

> AGENT

Now I see the actual bug. Reading dialog.tsx line 3:
> "Base UI releases focus scope and **body pointer-events** during close, not on unmount."

**Base UI already manages `body.style.pointerEvents` natively.** Our `syncBodyPointerEvents` in `overlayStack.ts` is fighting with it — two systems setting the same CSS on the same element at different times. Our code either locks after Base UI released (stays locked) or unlocks before Base UI's animation (bounces).

Fix: delete the body-pointer-events manipulation in our overlay stack. Base UI handles it.

> AGENT

Pushed as `1b9045cc5`. Pull and retry.

**Root cause**: two systems were setting `document.body.style.pointerEvents` — our `overlayStack.syncBodyPointerEvents` and Base UI's Dialog primitive natively. They raced on close. Before M7, my `isOverlayActuallyOpen` DOM heuristic had a timing bug that usually prevented our code from locking at all — so Base UI won by default and things worked. M7 correctly detects open state, both systems lock on open, and close-release races → stuck.

**Fix**: neutralized `syncBodyPointerEvents` to a no-op. Base UI is now the sole owner of `body.style.pointerEvents`. Our stack still does everything else (z-ordering, focus restoration, `isElementWithinKnownOverlay`) — just not body styles.

**Net diff**: 3 files changed, +18 / −53 (negative, which is what the state-ownership doc we just wrote tells us to prefer — one owner per state).

Tests: 4578/4578 green. The 3 tests that were asserting our ownership were updated to only check stack ordering + DOM presence.

This is exactly the kind of "two systems sharing one piece of state" bug the `state_ownership.md` doc from M7A was meant to warn against — just applied to a Base UI/our-stack boundary we hadn't considered.
